sentence: INTRODUCTION Estimating the likely ‘heavy hitters’ amongst the possible outcomes of an unknown probability distribution can be a useful primitive for several applications, ranging from clustering and natural language processing to network ﬂow / cache management and online advertising.
label: none

sentence: In this work, we formulate and study a Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) sequential estimation problem in which the learner has access to a stream of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples from an underlying unknown distribution over a given support set via an oracle which it can query.
label: none

sentence: The goal of the learner is to identify the set of elements in the support of the distribution whose probability value is above a pre-deﬁned threshold.
label: none

sentence: We will henceforth refer to this problem as threshold-based support identiﬁcation .
label: none

sentence: We consider two natural models for oracle queries: (a) direct query where the learner provides a sample index and the oracle responds with the value of the corresponding sample; and (b) pairwise query where the learner queries the oracle with a pair of indices and the oracle responds with a binary answer conﬁrming whether the sample values are identical or not.
label: none

sentence: Note that in the pairwise query model, the true values of the samples are not revealed.
label: none

sentence: While the former model has been a staple in the online learning literature [ 1 ], the latter has also received signiﬁcant attention recently under a wide variety of settings [ 2 ]–[ 6 ].
label: none

sentence: The broad goal of our work is to design query-efﬁcient schemes for these oracle models which can reliably estimate the support elements with probability values above a given threshold.
label: none

sentence: A concrete application of the above setting (and a key motivation for the formulation) can be found in a clustering problem where we have an underlying collection of items which can be partitioned into a given number of clusters based on some inherent property, for example, products in a shopping platform based on category or a population of individuals based on their political preferences.
label: none

sentence: However, unlike the usual setting where the goal is full clustering , i.e., mapping each individual item to its corresponding cluster [ 2 ], [ 7 ], we consider partial clustering where the goal is relaxed to identifying cluster indices with size larger than a certain fraction of the population.
label: none

sentence: Now, say a stream of samples is generated from the population by picking an item uniformly at random in each instant.
label: none

sentence: Then, it is easy to see that the probability of picking an item from a certain cluster is proportional to the size of the cluster and thus, the problem of identifying clusters with size greater than a fraction of the population would correspond to solving the threshold-based support identiﬁcation problem under the corresponding sampling distribution as mentioned above.
label: none

sentence: Our results provide schemes for performing partial clustering which can have signiﬁcantly smaller query complexity than the naive approach of performing full clustering and then selecting the appropriate clusters.
label: none

sentence: For example, say we have n √ items with a ground truth clustering with k = Θ( n ) clusters, where the three largest clusters have √ 7 / 8 size n and the remaining clusters are of size O ( n ) .
label: none

sentence: If we have to identify all the clusters with size more than n 3 / 4 with access to a pairwise oracle, Theorem 3 shows that this can be performed using O ( n ) queries whereas the naive approach would require O ( nk ) = O ( n 3 / 2 ) queries [ 5 ].
label: none

sentence: We make the following contributions to understanding the query complexity for this class of sequential estimation problems.
label: none

sentence: For both the query models, we ﬁrst design sequential algorithms which can provably solve the threshold-based support identiﬁcation problem with large probability and also provide upper bounds on their query complexity.
label: none

sentence: The estimators are based on maintaining empirical estimates and conﬁdence intervals for the probability values associated with each element of the support.
label: none

sentence: We also provide information-theoretic lower bounds on the query complexity of any reliable estimator under these query models.
label: none

sentence: The bounds presented are instance-speciﬁc, i.e., they depend on the underlying probability distribution and the value of the threshold.
label: none

sentence: Finally, we also consider noisy versions of both the direct query as well as the pairwise query models, and propose robust estimators which can effectively counter the noise in the oracle responses.
label: none

sentence: Related Work Estimation of properties of distributions using samples is a direction of work which has a long and rich history.
label: none

sentence: While some of the older works were concerned with the statistical properties of the estimators such as consistency etc., see for example [ 8 ], [ 9 ] which study mode estimation, there has been a lot of work recently on characterizing the optimal query complexity for estimating various properties of probability distributions including entropy [ 10 ], [ 11 ], support size and coverage [ 12 ], [ 13 ], and ‘Lipschitz’ properties [ 14 ] amongst others.
label: none

sentence: Another related line of work is the ‘heavy hitter’ estimation problem in the context of streaming algorithms [ 15 ]–[ 17 ] where given an arbitrary stream of samples from a large alphabet, the goal is to identify those symbols whose frequency is above a certain threshold.
label: none

sentence: The metric of performance is usually computational in nature such as the memory size, the number of passes or run time complexity.
label: none

sentence: In contrast to these works, we study the threshold-based support identiﬁcation problem in the stochastic setting and our interest is in deriving instance-speciﬁc bounds on optimal query complexity which illustrate the dependence on the underlying distribution.
label: none

sentence: Also, we study the query complexity for reliable estimation under several query models including the pairwise query model which isn’t as prevalent in the literature.
label: none

sentence: Online decision making and active learning are also key features of the popular framework of Multi-Armed Bandits (MABs) [ 18 ].
label: none

sentence: In particular, the problem of thresholding bandits [ 19 ] aims to ﬁnd the set of arms whose mean reward is above a certain threshold, using the minimum number of arm pulls.
label: none

sentence: Thinking of each element in the support set as an arm, the MAB problem is indeed quite related to the setting studied in this work, especially the one with pairwise queries and we explore this relationship in this paper.
label: none

sentence: One key difference between the MAB problem and our setup is that in the former we can choose to pull any arm at each instance, whereas in our problem the arm to be pulled is determined exogenously by the samples generated by the underlying probability distribution.
label: none

sentence: The goal in [ 2 ], [ 7 ] is to fully cluster a collection of items and they characterize the optimal query complexity 1 for this task.
label: none

sentence: In this context, our work corresponds to the less stringent objective of identifying the ‘signiﬁcantly large’ clusters which might be a natural objective in several unsupervised machine learning applications where we wish to associate labels to a large fraction of the unlabelled dataset and has not been studied before, to the best of our knowledge.
label: none

sentence: On the other hand, [ 20 ], [ 21 ] study the related problems of identifying the top- m clusters and mode of an underlying distribution and ﬁnd bounds on the optimal query complexity for these tasks.
label: none

sentence: While the broad structure of our algorithms and lower bound techniques are similar, the details differ greatly, for example in the choice of conﬁdence intervals in achievability and alternate instances for the converses.
label: none

sentence: One additional technical challenge that we face due to our different objective is that the number of clusters to be recovered is not ﬁxed apriori (all or one or m ), but depends on the particular problem instance and this requires careful treatment in the algorithms as well as in the analysis.
label: none

sentence: FuncNN : An R Package to Fit Deep Neural Networks Using Generalized Input Spaces Barinder Thind Sidi Wu Simon Fraser University Simon Fraser University Richard Groenewald Jiguo Cao Columbia University Simon Fraser University arXiv:2009.09111v2 [stat.ML] 22 Sep 2020 Abstract Neural networks have excelled at regression and classiﬁcation problems when the input space consists of scalar variables.
label: none

sentence: As a result of this proﬁciency, several popular packages have been developed that allow users to easily ﬁt these kinds of models.
label: none

sentence: However, the methodology has excluded the use of functional covariates and to date, there exists no software that allows users to build deep learning models with this generalized input space.
label: none

sentence: To the best of our knowledge, the functional neural network ( FuncNN ) library is the ﬁrst such package in any programming language; the library has been developed for R and is built on top of the keras architecture.
label: none

sentence: Throughout this paper, several functions are introduced that provide users an avenue to easily build models, generate predictions, and run cross-validations.
label: none

sentence: A summary of the underlying methodology is also presented.
label: none

sentence: The ultimate contribution is a package that provides a set of general modelling and diagnostic tools for data problems in which there exist both functional and scalar covariates.
label: none

sentence: Keywords : functional inputs, deep learning, R , keras . 1.
label: none

sentence: Introduction In recent years, deep learning methodologies have become the standard approach for predic- tion problems.
label: none

sentence: For example, He, Zhang, Ren, and Sun ( 2016 ) broke previous benchmarks by developing deep neural networks with over a hundred hidden layers; this was made possible by an innovation brought upon by a simple adjustment of the algorithm – adding the output of a previous layer back into the layers following it.
label: none

sentence: Another set of examples can be found in any one of the annual ImageNet Large-Scale Visual Recognition Challenges ( Krizhevsky, Sutskever, and Hinton 2012 ; Russakovsky, Deng, Su, Krause, Satheesh, Ma, Huang, Karpa- thy, Khosla, Bernstein et al. 2015 ) where neural networks are consistently on the podium.
label: none

sentence: These innovations naturally sparked the development of software that supplied users with an arsenal of tools to apply these methods.
label: none

sentence: There is a wide array of software available in multiple programming languages that implements a variety of methods in deep learning and neural networks.
label: none

sentence: For example, R packages nnet ( Venables and Ripley 2002 ) and neuralnet ( Fritsch, Guenther, and Wright 2019 ) are standard sets of tools in the training of and prediction from neural networks using the Broyden-Fletcher- 2 The FuncNN Package Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) algorithm and backpropagation, respectively.
label: none

sentence: Both of these allow for some ﬂexibility in terms of user selected activation functions and error measurements, but vastly more broad selections of tools are available within the RSNNS ( Bergmeir and Benítez 2012 ) and keras ( Allaire and Chollet 2020 ) application programming interfaces (API), which may be used in both R and Python .
label: none

sentence: Both of these make detailed user customization possible and are intended to facilitate the development of deep learning models and methodologies.
label: none

sentence: Central to this paper is functional data analysis (FDA), an area of modern applied statistics that has witnessed swift development due to its ability to deal with a large and distinct class of statistical problems.
label: none

sentence: In particular, it is often the case that data is collected at high resolution at many points in space or time, resembling and being treated as a smooth function - this is known as functional data.
label: none

sentence: FDA is used instead of the standard approach of analysing single points when we are interested in framing an analysis of a set of points as if they are samples from a speciﬁc curve.
label: none

sentence: Presently, the primary software for FDA in any programming language is the fda package ( Ramsay, Graves, and Hooker 2020 ) in R , designed to accompany the textbooks of Ramsay and Silverman ( 2005 ) and Ramsay, Hooker, and Graves ( 2009 ).
label: none

sentence: The main functionality within the package revolves around functional regression, allowing users to ﬁt regression models where one or several of the response and explanatory variables are functions instead of scalar valued.
label: none

sentence: Several packages in R build upon this base by extending standard statistical methods to functional data.
label: none

sentence: For example, funHDDC ( Schmutz and Bouveyron 2019 ) and funFEM ( Bouveyron 2015 ) handle functional clustering, FDboost ( Brockhaus and Ruegamer 2018 ) applies gradient boosting in functional regression and GPFDA ( Shi and Cheng 2014 ) incorporates functional regression as the mean response in Gaussian processes, among other packages.
label: none

sentence: Another library, fda.usc ( Febrero-Bande and Oviedo de la Fuente 2012 ), streamlines the ﬁtting process of many common functional modelling approaches such as non-parametric functional regression ( Ferraty and Vieu 2006 ) and functional partial least squares methods ( Aneiros-Pérez and Vieu 2006 ).
label: none

sentence: Additionally, the BFDA package ( Yang and Ren 2019 ) in MATLAB provides a library for Bayesian FDA.
label: none

sentence: To the best of our knowledge, the applications of these packages do not extend to include deep learning models.
label: none

sentence: For this reason, this paper introduces the FuncNN package, which allows users to include functions as input variables in neural networks and implements the theoretical discussion in Thind, Multani, and Cao ( 2020 ) and Rossi and Conan-Guez ( 2005 ).
label: none

sentence: This methodology has been shown to outperform many other functional and multivariate methods in a number of real world and simulated examples as seen in Thind et al. ( 2020 ).
label: none

sentence: The FuncNN package introduces several functions.
label: none

sentence: The primary function fnn.fit() , grants users the ability to eﬀortlessly generate models for their data; they also gain access to several customization options in the form of hyperparameters.
label: none

sentence: The output of this function can be acted upon by several other functions within the package such as fnn.predict() and fnn.fnc() which serve to be predictive and visualization functions.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, we introduce tuning and cross-validation functions aptly named fnn.tune() and fnn.cv() , respectively.
label: none

sentence: The package is readily available on CRAN can be installed as follows: R> install.packages("FuncNN") Or through GitHub using the devtools ( Wickham, Hester, and Chang 2020 ) package: R> devtools::install_github("b-thi/FuncNN") Barinder Thind, Sidi Wu, Richard Groenewald, Jiguo Cao 3 The rest of the article is organized as follows: Section 2 explores some of the theoretical background associated with the package.
label: none

sentence: In Section 3 , the bulk of the functions are pre- sented, including the model building and prediction functions; some visualization tools are also showcased with accompanying examples.
label: none

sentence: In Section 4 , helper functions such as those for cross-validation and tuning are detailed.
label: none

sentence: Lastly, Section 5 includes concluding thoughts and scheduled updates for the package. 2.

sentence: Pre-processing The FuncNN package allows two types of inputs of data; data can be passed in raw or pre-processed.
label: none

sentence: As with most functional data analysis coding, pre-processing is required to approximate the raw data x ( t ), using basis expansions.
label: none

sentence: However, this can be tedious and ul- timately, a barrier for anyone who is not familiar with the required procedures.
label: none

sentence: The FuncNN package provides a remedy by letting novice users input their data without the heavy lift- ing of converting it into its functional form while also granting the opportunity for further customization for users who require a more speciﬁc or specialized pre-processing.
label: none

sentence: In the case where the data is passed in raw, the FuncNN package will do a simple pre-processing using a Fourier basis expansion with 31 terms.
label: none

sentence: While this is an average-case compromise that mini- mizes initial eﬀort, the alternative approach of pre-processing allows for greater ﬂexibility in the development of x ( t ).
label: none

sentence: Since the functional observations can be passed in two diﬀerent ways, they can be one of two object types.
label: none

sentence: In the raw case, the functional covariates are passed in as a K -dimensional list where each element of the list is an N × p data.frame() containing p measurements over the domain for each of the N subjects.
label: none

sentence: R> func_cov_list = list(func_cov_1, func_cov_2, ..., func_cov_K) The scalar covariates can be passed in similar to most predictive functions i.e., as an N × J matrix containing information on the J scalar variables for each of the N observations.
label: none

label: none

sentence: In R , the tensor-type object exists as an array() .
label: none

sentence: The dimensionality of the tensor will be × × M k N K where each row corresponds to the estimated coeﬃcient when the basis expansion was made, each column is an individual observation, and each “slice” corresponds to one of the K functional covariates.

sentence: A PREPRINT - O CTOBER 14, 2020 1 Introduction The availability of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data has steadily increased, with demand for relevant analytical methods increasing accordingly.
label: none

sentence: Useful for describing brain activity, the blood oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) signal underlying fMRI serves as a surrogate for neuronal activity [Menon et al., 1992].
label: none

sentence: These BOLD signals are often collected at thousands of three-dimensional cubes called voxels across time, yielding high-dimensional data.
label: none

sentence: Dimension reduction prior to analysis is often done by averaging activation levels within sets of voxels called regions of interest (ROIs).
label: none

sentence: Using these ROIs, one approach for analyzing fMRI data is to describe functional connectivity (FC), deﬁned as the temporal dependence of neuronal activity in regions of the brain [Friston et al., 1993].
label: none

sentence: For resting-state fMRI data from a single subject, graphical modeling approaches have commonly been used for joint analysis of FC connections among a set of ROIs [Lee et al., 2013, Smitha et al., 2017].
label: none

sentence: Gaussian graphical models (GGM) assume a multivariate Gaussian distribution for the BOLD signals, under which the inverse covariance matrix, called the precision matrix, conveys conditional dependencies between ROIs [Lauritzen, 2004], and is used to describe FC through a graphical representation of the ROI dependence structure.
label: none

sentence: Speciﬁcally, an undirected graph is constructed with nodes representing ROIs, and edges connecting pairs of conditionally dependent nodes.
label: none

sentence: In this setting, methods for estimating sparse precision matrices have been used to obtain the FC structure among ROIs for a single subject.
label: none

sentence: One commonly used method is the graphical lasso or GLasso [Friedman et al., 2007].
label: none

sentence: For multi-subject fMRI data, there are often shared features of FC across subjects that can be accounted for to improve estimation.
label: none

sentence: However, these methods do not account for between-subject heterogeneity in FC structures that is commonly present [Fiecas et al., 2017, Price et al., 2017].
label: none

sentence: This heterogeneity among subjects could be due to the presence of multiple subgroups or clusters of subjects with varying FC patterns [Mueller et al., 2013].
label: none

sentence: Although extensive work has been done on methods for classifying subjects based on resting-state and task-based fMRI signals [Davatzikos et al., 2005, Calhoun et al., 2008, Shen et al., 2010, Arribas et al., 2010, Castro et al., 2014], fewer studies have focused on unsupervised clustering of subjects based on FC patterns.
label: none

sentence: Using an unsupervised maximum margin clustering method, Zeng et al. [2014] distinguished depressed patients from healthy controls based on FC estimates obtained from pairwise correlations.
label: none

sentence: However, the maximum margin clustering approach does not yield interpretable estimates of FC network structures for each class or subject which are of clinical importance.
label: none

sentence: Motivated by gene network analysis of microarray data, penalized Gaussian mixture models (GMM) have been proposed for simultaneous subject clustering and multiple network estimation [Zhou et al., 2009, Hill and Mukherjee, 2013, Gao et al., 2016, Hao et al., 2018].
label: none

sentence: However, these methods apply to subject clustering with only one observation per subject as often seen in gene expression data and assume a common covariance matrix for observations within a cluster.
label: none

sentence: Thus, they are not applicable to multi-subject fMRI data which have multiple observations per subject, and they do not allow for within-cluster heterogeneity. 2 A PREPRINT - O CTOBER 14, 2020 In this paper, we propose a penalized model-based clustering method for resting-state fMRI data which groups patients based on FC features.
label: none

sentence: Speciﬁcally, we propose a random covariance clustering method (RCCM) to simultaneously cluster subjects and obtain sparse precision matrix estimates for each cluster as well as each subject, producing interpretable estimates of subject- and group-level FC networks.
label: none

sentence: A major contribution of the RCCM over existing penalized model-based clustering methods is to allow for clustering of entire subsets of fMRI data observed for each subject, rather than only individual observations, and that it allows subjects within each cluster to have similar but not identical FC networks.
label: none

sentence: This is implemented via a hierarchical structure, in which the subject-level precision matrices follow a mixture of Wishart distributions, each with mean matrix equal to a corresponding cluster-level precision matrix.
label: none

sentence: Using a mixture of Wishart distributions for each subject’s precision matrix rather than a Gaussian mixture for individual observations retains observations together for each participant.
label: none

sentence: This is necessary for clustering participants based on fMRI data since it would not be interpretable to have observations from a single participant separated into multiple clusters.
label: none

sentence: The degrees of freedom of each Wishart component controls the level of similarity between each subject-level matrix and its corresponding group-level matrix and is treated as a tuning parameter which is selected via an extended stability approach to regularization selection (stARS) method described in Section 2.3.
label: none

sentence: Our simulations provide evidence that by conducting concurrent clustering and network estimation our proposed RCCM has improved performance in the estimation of subject-level networks due to sharing information across similar subjects, while better clustering is achieved due to improved subject-level estimates.
label: none

sentence: We applied the RCCM to a resting-state fMRI data set collected on 61 participants diagnosed with schizophrenia and 43 healthy controls, ﬁnding a slight tendency for participants diagnosed with schizophrenia to be clustered together.
label: none

sentence: For the rest of the paper, we present the proposed RCCM, the computational algorithm, and the selection of tuning parameters and the number of clusters in Section 2.
label: none

sentence: Then, we describe simulations conducted to explore the relative performance of the RCCM to competitive two-step methods in Section 3 and illustrate the utility of the RCCM on a resting-state fMRI data set in Section 4.
label: none

sentence: Lastly, in Section 5 we conclude with a discussion of our ﬁndings. 2 Method 2.1 Random Covariance Clustering Model We consider the setting in which we have collected fMRI data on K subjects for p different ROIs with n observations or time points on the k th subject.

sentence: Keywords: Consistent ensemble; Diversity penalty; High-dimensional classification; Logistic regres- sion models; Split modeling. 1 1 Introduction The surge of genomic data collection through ever-evolving technologies has necessitated the de- velopment of sophisticated statistical methods to analyze high-dimensional gene expression data, unlocking its potential for breakthroughs in healthcare and scientific discovery.
label: none

sentence: In many medical genomics applications, the goal is to train a classifier that can accurately predict the presence of a disease or particular subtypes of a disease based on the genetic profile of a patient.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, in the medical sciences and other fields predictions often have important consequences in decision- making processes, so there is a high demand for interpretable learning methods (see e.g. Murdoch et al. , 2019 ; Rudin , 2019 ; Rudin et al. , 2022 ).
label: none

sentence: It should thus be clear how a classifier arrives at its predictions so that decisions can be fully explained.
label: none

sentence: In addition, medical researchers aim to unravel the relation between the genetic profile and occurrence of a disease, so an appropriate classification method should also be able to identify patterns between the expression of key biomarkers and the presence of a disease.
label: none

sentence: The vast richness and availability of medical genomics data is evident from large publicly accessible databases such as the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database ( Edgar et al. , 2002 ; Barrett et al. , 2012 ).
label: none

sentence: In many of these datasets, a large number of gene expression measurements are collected for a relatively small number of (cell tissue) samples.
label: none

sentence: The status of the sample is typically given as well, specifying e.g. whether the sample collected was affected by a disease or not.
label: none

sentence: Classification methods can then be used to discover patterns between the expression level of certain genes and the presence of the disease.
label: none

sentence: The two types of methods that are generally deployed in such applications are sparse and ensemble methods, respectively.
label: none

sentence: On the one hand, sparse methods yield interpretable models that only use a subset of the genes to make a decision (see e.g. Hastie et al. , 2015 , for a modern treatment of sparse methods).
label: none

sentence: How- ever, because the number of predictor genes is much larger than the number of samples, there may be several models comprised of different subsets of genes that are equally accurate in predicting the presence of the disease (a phenomenon coined “the multiplicity of good models” by McCul- lagh and Nelder , 1989 ).
label: none

sentence: Thus, several potentially important genes may be erroneously discarded from the decision-making process when using a single sparse model.
label: none

sentence: On the other hand, ensemble methods combine multiple diverse models and generally achieve superior prediction performance if the members of the ensemble are sufficiently diverse.
label: none

sentence: Ensemble methods have been particularly successful in high-dimensional prediction tasks with genomic data (see e.g. Dorani et al. , 2018 ; Zahoor and Zafar , 2020 ).
label: none

sentence: However, while ad hoc methods have been developed to assess variable importance in some ensemble methods, such as the variable importance measure of Breiman ( 2001 ), interpretation of the resulting prediction rules and identification of important predictor genes (i.e. key biomarkers) is less straightforward.
label: none

sentence: We propose a new approach to learn a diverse ensemble of sparse classification models that is especially well suited for high-dimensional medical genomics applications.
label: none

sentence: Specifically, we extend the regression ensemble method proposed by Christidis et al. ( 2020 ) to the binary classification setting.
label: none

sentence: We demonstrate the advantage of the proposed ensemble method in terms of both predic- tion and identification of key biomarkers using cancer genomics datasets from the GEO database, with a broader analysis including datasets for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis provided in the sup- plementary material.
label: none

sentence: In particular, we show that the prediction accuracy of the sparse models in the ensembles matches the prediction accuracy of standard single-model sparse methods.
label: none

sentence: Since the models in the ensembles are learned simultaneously and directly from the data (free of randomiza- tion or other heuristics) by optimizing a global objective function, they each provide an alternative 2 explanation for the relationship between the genes and disease.
label: none

sentence: The objective function contains a penalty that promotes diversity in the obtained models so that individual models may be driven by potentially different biological mechanisms.
label: none

sentence: With respect to the identification of important predictor genes, the examples demonstrate that the proposed ensemble method can identify key biomarkers that are discarded by state-of-the-art sparse methods and ensemble variable ranking methods.
label: none

sentence: At the same time, we show that the proposed method generally includes key biomarkers selected by sparse methods or flagged as important by ensemble variable ranking methods.
label: none

sentence: Each of the models in the proposed ensemble method is a penalized logistic regression with a sparsity inducing penalty such as the Lasso ( Donoho and Johnstone , 1994 ; Tibshirani , 1996 ) or the elastic net ( Zou and Hastie , 2005 ).
label: none

sentence: Rather than resorting to randomization or other indirect methods to generate different models, we jointly learn the models in the ensemble on the training data and incorporate a diversity penalty ( Christidis et al. , 2020 ) in the objective function with the aim to diversify the models.
label: none

sentence: The degree to which these models are sparse and diverse is driven directly by the data.
label: none

sentence: In this way, the method efficiently exploits the so-called accuracy- diversity trade-off between the models, and generates an ensemble with high predictive performance that often matches or even outperforms popular state-of-the-art ensemble methods.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, by ensembling the models at the level of their linear predictors we retain interpretability for the logistic regression coefficients in the ensembled model.
label: none

sentence: We use several measures of diversity ( Kuncheva and Whitaker , 2003 ) to study the accuracy-diversity trade-off in the ensemble method.
label: none

sentence: This trade- off provides insight in the effect of the number of ensembled models on the performance of the resulting ensemble.
label: none

sentence: This insight makes it possible to make some recommendations for the choice of the number of ensembled models.
label: none

sentence: Following the methodological development framework of Heinze et al. ( 2024 ), this work encom- passes phases I and II, introducing a novel method with initial validation through comprehensive simulations across various scenarios (sample sizes, sparsity, correlation structures, class imbalance, non-linearity, and interactions).
label: none

sentence: While the results of the numerical experiments and medical ge- nomics data applications demonstrate the promising performance of the proposed classification ensembles across a variety of data scenarios, we present this work as a method development study with strong proof-of-concept validation, rather than a claim of universal superiority.
label: none

sentence: The success observed across these carefully chosen testing scenarios suggests that phases III and IV, indepen- dent validation and practical implementation, may naturally follow as the method gains adoption in the research community.

label: none

sentence: This p > n scenario is common in bioinformatics and other fields.
label: none

sentence: To address these challenges, two primary families of methods have emerged as dominant strategies in the literature: sparse modeling, which aims for feature selection and interpretability, and ensemble methods, which typically focus on maximizing predictive accuracy and stability by combining multiple models.

sentence: AGGLIO : Global Optimization for Locally Convex Functions Debojyoti Dey Bhaskar Mukhoty Purushottam Kar IIT Kanpur { debojyot,bhaskarm,purushot } @cse.iitk.ac.in arXiv:2111.03932v1 [math.OC] 6 Nov 2021 November 9, 2021 Abstract This paper presents AGGLIO (Accelerated Graduated Generalized LInear-model Optimization), a stage-wise, graduated optimization technique that oﬀers global convergence guarantees for non-convex optimization problems whose objectives oﬀer only local convexity and may fail to be even quasi-convex at a global scale.
label: none

sentence: In particular, this includes learning problems that utilize popular activation functions such as sigmoid, softplus and SiLU that yield non-convex training objectives.
label: none

sentence: AGGLIO can be readily implemented using point as well as mini-batch SGD updates and oﬀers provable convergence to the global optimum in general conditions.
label: none

sentence: In experiments, AGGLIO outperformed several recently proposed optimization techniques for non-convex and locally convex objectives in terms of convergence rate as well as convergent accuracy.
label: none

sentence: AGGLIO relies on a graduation technique for generalized linear models, as well as a novel proof strategy, both of which may be of independent interest.
label: none

sentence: Code for AGGLIO is available at the following repository [link] . 1 Introduction The Generalized Linear Model (GLM) [ 22 ] provides a convenient extension to the linear regression model by allowing responses to be transformed using an inverse link function.
label: none

sentence: More speciﬁcally, given a covariate x ∈ R d and a gold linear model w ∈ R d , the corresponding response y ∈ R is generated such that ∗ E [ y ] = g − 1 ( x ⊤ w ) , ∗ − R R where g 1 : → is the inverse link function.
label: none

sentence: GLMs play a central role in machine learning, allowing predictions to be made across a variety of label spaces: using the identity link retrieves least squares regression for real-valued labels, the logit link oﬀers logistic regression for binary-valued labels, whereas the logarithmic link yields Poisson regression for count-valued labels.
label: none

sentence: The classical GLM is canonically associated with a unique likelihood distribution of the exponential family that allows eﬃcient model estimation via likelihood maximization (e.g., using the IRLS method).
label: none

sentence: The consistency properties of such M-estimators is well studied [ 1 , 19 ].
label: none

sentence: However, contemporary applications frequently forgo this canonical association in favor of a direct modelling as y = φ ( x ⊤ w ) + ϵ, (1) ∗ where w is the gold model, φ : R → R is an activation function and ϵ captures model mis-speciﬁcation and ∗ statistical noise.
label: none

sentence: This is especially true when GLMs are recursively applied to yield deep “neural” models which popularly use activation functions such as the sigmoid, the ReLU [ 21 ] and its variants e.g. leaky ReLU [ 18 ], softplus [ 9 ], GeLU and SiLU [ 13 ].
label: none

sentence: Indeed, no nice exponential family likelihood distribution exists corresponding to the ReLU-style activation functions such as GeLU, SiLU etc. 1 n In such situations, given data { ( x , y ) } generated using the mechanism speciﬁed in ( 1 ), instead of i i i =1 performing likelihood maximization to recover the gold model w , it is common to use a task-speciﬁc loss ∗ function to perform model recovery.
label: none

sentence: For instance, the squared loss could be used for regression problems, n 1 w ˆ = arg min X ( y − φ ( x ⊤ w )) 2 , (2) w ∈ R d i i n i =1 binary cross entropy could be used for classiﬁcation, etc. However, objective functions of the form in ( 2 ) are non-convex for most activation functions, including sigmoid, ReLU, and its variants.
label: none

sentence: This problem is magniﬁed for recursive GLMs giving rise to the challenge of training deep networks provably accurately.
label: none

sentence: This paper shows that for a wide range of popular activation functions, objectives such as those presented in ( 2 ) are actually locally convex around their global optimum, in fact strongly so.
label: none

sentence: However, this strong convexity is restricted to a tiny neighborhood around the optimum and thus, cannot be directly exploited in practice (since the objective function is decidedly non-convex at a global scale).
label: none

sentence: The paper ﬁrst establishes a more robust version of this result that shows that by graduating the activation function appropriately, this coveted neighborhood of strong convexity can be expanded, allowing standard GD to oﬀer a linear rate of convergence to the global optimum.
label: none

sentence: However, this expansion comes at a cost of diminished gradients that slow down the progress of descent algorithms such as GD/SGD.
label: none

sentence: Balancing these two opposing eﬀects using an adaptive graduation schedule yields AGGLIO .
label: none

sentence: This paper develops the AGGLIO method that oﬀers convergence to the global optimum at a linear rate for several GLM problems of the kind presented in ( 2 ).
label: none

sentence: The paper introduces novel concepts of Extendable Local Strong Convexity (ELSC) and proof techniques that may ﬁnd independent application to other problems.
label: none

sentence: In experiments, AGGLIO outperforms several recently proposed optimization techniques for locally convex objectives in terms of convergence rate as well as the accuracy of the ﬁnal model. 2 Related Works Non-convex Optimization.

sentence: The problem areas of compressive sensing, sparse recovery, and matrix completion were among the ﬁrst non-convex problems to be studied in great detail, giving rise to rich literature focusing on relaxation techniques such as LASSO [ 10 ] as well as iterative techniques such as IHT [ 3 ].

sentence: More recent work has broadened the scope to general-purpose non-convex optimization, partly due to the need to understand the training of deep models better.

sentence: Keywords– Langevin algorithm, SGLD, Markovian neural network, Stochastic control, Deep neural net- work, Stochastic optimization 1 Introduction Stochastic Optimal Control (SOC), which consists in optimizing a functional of a trajectory of a controlled Stochastic Diﬀerential Equation (SDE) has applications in a wide range of problems: management of resources, queuing systems, epidemic and population processes, pricing of ﬁnancial derivatives, portfolio allocation...
label: none

sentence: In comparison with classic optimal control, SOC models include a random noise with known probability distribution that aﬀects the evolution or the observation of the system.
label: none

sentence: SOC also aims at managing the risk induced by this noise.
label: none

sentence: SOC problems are usually solved using speciﬁc strategies, such as Forward-Backward SDEs (FBSDEs) [ PW99 ], or by solving Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) optimality conditions [ Bel57 ] through partial diﬀerential equations methods using appropriate numerical schemes or by stochastic dynamic programming [ KD01 ].
label: none

sentence: Such problems can also be solved using Neural Networks calibrated by SGD techniques [ GM05 , HE16 , WLP + 19 , CL21 , BHLP22 ].
label: none

sentence: More speciﬁcally, in this article we consider the numerical resolution of a SOC problem where the control is parametrized by a neural network calibrated by gradient descent.
label: none

sentence: This method implies to compute the path- wise derivatives along the trajectory of the SDE of the objective function with respect to the parameters of the neural network, as introduced in [ GG05 , Gil07 ].
label: none

sentence: Stochastic gradient descent is a very general approach that can be applied to a wide range of problems and which does not need to be speciﬁcally adapted to each problem under consideration.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, SGD scales very eﬃciently to high-dimensional problems, in contrast with HJB-based methods, and has proved its eﬃciency on highly non-convex problems [ DdVB15 ].
label: none

sentence: However, if the neural control is applied at many time steps as it is the case for the Euler-Maruyama scheme where the (discrete) control is taken as an approximation of a continuous control, then the SOC problem reads as the optimization of a very deep neural network, which is roughly as deep as the number of instants at which the control can be applied (see Figures 1 and 2 ).
label: none

sentence: Very deep neural networks are known to be considerably + more diﬃcult to train [ GB10 , DPG 14 ] and may run into vanishing gradient problems [ Hoc91 , Han18 ].
label: none

sentence: Indeed, the deeper the neural network is, the more non-linear it is, thus increasing the number of local traps for the gradient descent such as local (but not global) and saddle points.
label: none

sentence: In image analysis where very deep convolutional neural networks are commonly used, residual [ HZRS16 ] and convolutional dense [ HLVDMW17 ] networks were introduced to deal with this issue.
label: none

sentence: These networks are based on architectures with residual connections to propagate the gradient information through the numerous successive layers.
label: none

sentence: As it comes to deep SOC, we cannot freely change the structure of the neural network since it is ﬁxed by the equations deﬁning the SOC problem and therefore we cannot directly use residual connections.

sentence: We propose and analyze an objective function derived from a Bayesian formulation for learning a hidden Markov model with stochastic dynamics.
label: none

sentence: We then analyze this objective function in the context of several state-of-the-art approaches for both linear and nonlinear system ID.
label: none

sentence: In the former, we analyze least squares approaches for Markov parameter estimation, and in the latter, we analyze the multiple shooting approach.
label: none

sentence: We demonstrate the limitations of the optimization problems posed by these existing methods by showing that they can be seen as special cases of the proposed optimization objective under certain simplifying assumptions: conditional independence of data and zero model error.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, we observe that our proposed approach has improved smoothness and inherent regularization that make it well-suited for system ID and provide mathematical explanations for these characteristics’ origins.
label: none

sentence: Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate a mean squared error over 8.7 times lower compared to multiple shooting when data are noisy and/or sparse.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, the proposed approach can identify accurate and generalizable models even when there are more parameters than data or when the underlying system exhibits chaotic behavior.

sentence: Polyp-SAM: Transfer SAM for Polyp Segmentation Yuheng Li a , Mingzhe Hu b and Xiaofeng Yang a,b,c* a Department of Biomedical Engineering, Emory University, GA, Atlanta, USA b Department of Computer Science and Informatics, Emory University, GA, Atlanta, USA c Department of Radiation Oncology, Winship Cancer Institute, School of Medicine, Emory University, GA, Atlanta, USA *Email: xiaofeng.yang@emory.edu Abstract Colon polyps are considered important precursors for colorectal cancer.
label: none

sentence: Automatic segmentation of colon polyps can significantly reduce the misdiagnosis of colon cancer and improve physician annotation efficiency.
label: none

sentence: While many methods have been proposed for polyp segmentation, training large-scale segmentation networks with limited colonoscopy data remains a challenge.
label: none

sentence: Recently, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) has recently gained much attention in both natural and medical image segmentation.
label: none

sentence: SAM demonstrates superior performance in several image benchmarks and therefore shows great potential for medical image segmentation.
label: none

sentence: In this study, we propose Poly-SAM, a finetuned SAM model for polyp segmentation, and compare its performance to several state-of-the- art polyp segmentation models.
label: none

sentence: We also compare two transfer learning strategies of SAM with and without finetuning its encoders.
label: none

sentence: Evaluated on five public datasets, our Polyp-SAM achieves state-of- the-art performance on two datasets and impressive performance on three datasets, with dice scores all above 88%.
label: none

sentence: This study demonstrates the great potential of adapting SAM to medical image segmentation tasks.
label: none

sentence: We plan to release the code and model weights for this paper at: https://github.com/ricklisz/Polyp-SAM . 1.
label: none

sentence: Introduction Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common gastrointestinal malignancy with high morbidity and a low 5- year survival rate if diagnosed late.
label: none

sentence: CRC is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths in United States with more than 106,180 cases and 52,580 deaths in 2022 [1].
label: none

sentence: The prescence of Colon polyp is an important factor in causing CRC.
label: none

sentence: Early detection and removal of CRC can significantly reduce the mortality rate and improve patient outcomes [2].
label: none

sentence: Colonoscopy is considered the gold standard for CRC diagnosis.
label: none

sentence: It can identify and eliminate colorectal polyps, which can prevent further damage to the surrounding tissues and lower the chance of CRC.
label: none

sentence: Currently, the screening of colorectal polyps relies on manual inspection of endoscopic images.
label: none

sentence: However, this method is tedious and time-consuming, and subject to clinician’s inter-reader variability.
label: none

sentence: Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) for colonoscopy can effectively improve annotation efficiency and reduce time-to-diagnosis [3].
label: none

sentence: Recent advances in deep learning models have resulted in many neural networks for medical image segmentation.
label: none

sentence: One of the most popular architectures is U-Net [4], a convolutional neural network with an encoder path and a decoder path.
label: none

sentence: The encoder path captures the context of the image producing feature maps and it is made up of a stack of convolution and max pooling layers.
label: none

sentence: The decoder path enables precise localization using transposed convolutions.
label: none

sentence: Zhou et al. presented U-Net++ [5], which is a nested architecture for medical image segmentation.
label: none

sentence: However, annotation time and costs remain significant obstacles for collecting and curating medical datasets to train large-scale segmentation models, primarily because trained physicians must typically provide careful mask annotations for images.
label: none

sentence: Transfer learning leverages the knowledge learned from large-scale natural image datasets to solve specific problems in the medical domain [6, 7].
label: none

sentence: Recent advances in large foundational language models such as Chat-GPT and GPT-4 have shown impressive performances in various language tasks [8].
label: none

sentence: With their superior transferability to different tasks, many have explored transferring foundational language models to medical tasks [9, 10].
label: none

sentence: Segment Anything Model (SAM) is proposed as a foundation model for image segmentation that generates high-quality object masks from input prompts (e.g., points, boxes, and masks) [11].
label: none

sentence: Due to its promising performance in several computer vision benchmarks, SAM has attracted much attention in medical image segmentation [12-14].
label: none

sentence: In this paper, we propose Poly-SAM, a foundational vision model for polyp segmentation using transfer learning.
label: none

sentence: We finetune SAM on a collection of multi-center colonoscopy images.
label: none

sentence: We show that with our finetuned SAM can outperform existing methods for polyp segmentation and demonstrate superior generalizability to multi-institutional data. 2.
label: none

sentence: Method 2.1 Datasets To validate the effectiveness of our finetuning method, we conducted comparison experiments on five benchmark colonoscopy datasets: 1) Kvasir [15]: This dataset was collected by Vestre Viken Health Trust in Norway and consisting of 1,000 polyp images and their corresponding ground truth from colonoscopy video sequences.
label: none

sentence: The ground truth was manually annotated by medical doctors and then verified by experienced gastroenterologists.
label: none

sentence: The resolution of the images varies from 332 × 487 to 1920 × 1072 pixels. 2) CVC-ClinicDB [16]: This dataset contains 612 images collected from 29 colonoscopy video sequences with a resolution of 288×384.
label: none

sentence: It was built in collaboration with the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona, Spain. 3) CVC-ColonDB [17]: This dataset consists of 380 polyp images and their corresponding ground truth with a resolution of 500×570.
label: none

sentence: The images were generated from 15 different videos from which experts guaranteed that the extracted frames showed an obviously different viewpoint by rejecting similar frames and annotated the 380 frames manually. 4) ETIS [16] This dataset contains 196 polyp images with a size of 966 × 1225. 5).
label: none

sentence: CVC-300 [17]: This dataset includes 60 polyp images with a resolution of 500×574.
label: none

sentence: For fair comparison to previous studies, we followed the same data split settings in [18], using 900 images from Kvasir and 550 ones from CVC- ClinicDB to form the training set.
label: none

sentence: Segment Anything Segment Anything Model (SAM) is a model that segments user-defined objects of interest with user prompts such as point, mask, bounding box, or text.
label: none

sentence: SAM will also return a segmentation mask even if the prompt is missing or ambiguous.
label: none

sentence: SAM has three components: an image encoder, a prompt encoder and a mask decoder.
label: none

sentence: The image encoder of SAM uses a masked autoencoder (MAE) that has been modified to handle input images of up to 1024x1024 resolution.
label: none

sentence: The ViT backbone consists of a series of self-attention layers to capture long-range dependencies between patches of the input and the the input image.
label: none

sentence: This is followed by a set of feedforward layers that transform the output of the self- attention layers into a set of feature maps used by the mask decoder to generate segmentation masks.
label: none

sentence: The prompt encoders are tailored for different user inputs such as points, boxes, texts, and masks.
label: none

sentence: Each point is encoded by Fourier positional encoding and two learnable tokens for specifying foreground and background, respectively.
label: none

sentence: The bounding box is encoded by the point encoding of its top-left corner and bottom-right corner.
label: none

sentence: The free-form text is encoded by the pre-trained text-encoder in CLIP.
label: none

sentence: The mask prompt has the same spatial resolution as the input image, which is encoded by convolution feature maps.
label: none

sentence: Finally, the mask decoder employs a lightweight design, which consists of two transformer layers with a dynamic mask prediction head and an Intersection-over-Union (IoU) score regression head.
label: none

sentence: The mask prediction head can generate three 4× downscaled masks, which correspond to the whole object, part, and subpart of the object.
label: none

sentence: SAM was trained using SA-1B dataset which was developed in three stages.
label: none

sentence: First, a set of images was annotated by human annotators by clicking on objects and manually refining masks generated by SAM which at that point was trained using public datasets.
label: none

sentence: Second, the annotators were asked to segment masks that were not confidently generated by SAM to increase the diversity of objects.
label: none

sentence: The final set of masks was generated automatically by prompting the SAM model with a set of points distributed in a grid across the image and selecting confident and stable masks.
label: none

sentence: SA-1B includes more than 1B masks from 11M licensed and privacy-preserving image.
label: none

sentence: This dataset has 400× more masks than any existing segmentation dataset, resulting in a high potential for being able to segment objects of types that it has not seen during training, i.e., zero-shot learning ability. 2.3 Preprocessing and Prompt generation Since the SAM encoder requires high-resolution input, each image was resized to 3×1024×1024 before training.
label: none

sentence: The output masks from the SAM decoder were then resized to the original resolution of the image.
label: none

sentence: Down-sampled masks were compared to the ground truth masks to calculate loss.
label: none

sentence: SAM relies on accurate prompts to generate high-quality masks.
label: none

sentence: Previous investigations of SAM demonstrated that the bounding box is the most effective prompt for SAM.
label: none

sentence: In our experiments, only the Kvasir dataset provided ground truth bounding boxes for each patient.
label: none

sentence: For the remaining two datasets, we automatically extracted the bounding boxes from the ground truth masks.
label: none

sentence: During training and evaluation, we directly utilized the bounding boxes to prompt SAM to generate polyp masks. 2.4 Polyp-SAM: Transfer SAM for polyp segmentation To fully explore SAM's potential for medical image segmentation, we propose two strategies for transfer learning SAM (Fig. 1): 1) Pretraining only the mask decoder while freezing all encoders; 2) Pretraining the image encoder, prompt encoder, and mask decoder.
label: none

sentence: For the base model, we evaluate both strategies using ViT-B.
label: none

sentence: Next, we aim to finetune SAM’s two base models (ViT-B and ViT-L) for polyp segmentation (Polyp-SAM-B and Polyp-SAM-L).
label: none

sentence: During this step, we finetuned all components of SAM.
label: none

sentence: We trained using an effective batch size of 48 with gradient accumulation.
label: none

sentence: The loss function used was a simple Dice Loss commonly used in segmentation tasks.
label: none

sentence: We optimized using AdamW and used a learning rate scheduler with linear warm-up and cosine annealing.
label: none

sentence: The learning rate was set at 4e-6.
label: none

sentence: During training, we used only 80% of the data while the remaining 20% was used for validation to restore the best weights.
label: none

sentence: The PC used to fine-tune the model has an x86_64 architecture with 12 CPUs, 6 cores per socket, and 2 sockets, for a total of 24 threads.
label: none

sentence: The CPU model is an Intel Xeon E5-2603 v4 @ 1.70GHz with 30MB L3 cache.
label: none

sentence: The system has a 46-bit physical and 48-bit virtual address size and supports virtualization via VT-x.
label: none

sentence: The GPU is a Tesla V100-PCIE with 2 cards, each with a memory capacity of 32GB.
label: none

sentence: For evaluation, we used the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) to evaluate the region overlap ratio between the ground truth and segmentation results, which are two commonly used segmentation metrics in polyp segmentation. mIoU measures the mean overlap between the predicted and ground truth masks by dividing the intersection of the masks by the union of the masks.
label: none

sentence: DSC also measures the overlap between the predicted and ground truth masks, which is calculated by computing the harmonic mean of the precision and recall scores.
label: none

sentence: Our proposed transfer learning strategies for Poly-SAM. a).
label: none

sentence: We freeze SAM’s image encoder and prompt encoder and finetune only mask decoder. b).
label: none

sentence: We finetune both encoders and decoder. 3.
label: none

sentence: Result 3.1 Comparison of transfer learning strategies We first compared the results of our two transfer learning strategies on Polyp-SAM-B using a multi- center dataset.
label: none

sentence: As shown in Table 1, our model demonstrated better performance when all components were fine-tuned.
label: none

sentence: However, we observed that the gains from fine-tuning all components were limited (0-3% in DSC and 0.1-4% in mIoU) compared to fine-tuning only the mask decoder.
label: none

sentence: Therefore, it remains an open question whether SAM's encoders should be fine-tuned to achieve optimal performance.
label: none

sentence: Finetuning all components of SAM consistently leads to better performance metrics.
label: none

sentence: Our first study followed the data split strategy in [17] using mixed images from CVC-ColonDB, Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-300, and ETIS.
label: none

sentence: The polyp segmentation metrics of all the compared algorithms on the test set are shown in Table 2.
label: none

sentence: Our Polyp-SAM-B achieved state-of-the-art results in CVC-Colon DB (89.4% DSC), CVC-300 (92.4% DSC), and ETIS (90.3% DSC), outperforming all comparable methods.
label: none

sentence: Polyp-SAM-B also achieved comparable results with other methods in CVC-ClinicalDB and Kvasir.
label: none

sentence: Polyp-SAM-L achieved state- of-the-art results in CVC-300 with 92.9% DSC and 88.9% mIoU, and in ETIS with 90.5% DSC and 86.0% mIoU.
label: none

sentence: Visualization of Polyp-SAM’s segmentation results from mixed datasets are shown in Figure 2 and Figure 3.
label: none

sentence: In general, we find that both Polyp-SAM-B and Polyp-SAM-L perform reasonably well across multi-center data.
label: none

sentence: We also show some cases where Polyp-SAM fails to detect lesions in Figure 4.
label: none

sentence: We suspect that Polyp-SAM still requires further finetuning in the case of multiple sporadic lesions.
label: none

sentence: This result demonstrates Polyp-SAM's superior generalizability across different datasets.When using Colon-DB as the testing set, we noticed that Poly-SAM-B's performance did not increase when trained on more data (i.e., CVC-ClinicDB and CVC-300).

sentence: Polyp- SAM-L gained a 0.8% increase in DSC and a 1.3% increase in mIoU.

sentence: Discussion and conclusion In this paper, we propose Polyp-SAM, a foundational model for polyp segmentation using colonoscopy images by finetuning SAM.
label: none

sentence: Both Polyp-SAM-B and Polyp-SAM-L demonstrate excellent performance across five public colon polyp datasets when compared to existing methods.
label: none

sentence: Although Polyp-SAM-L is much more computationally complex, we note that it did not outperform the lightweight Polyp-SAM-B in three out of five public datasets during finetuning.
label: none

sentence: This result led us to believe that the lightweight ViT-B model of SAM is more suitable to be transferred to medical image applications.
label: none

sentence: We also compare two strategies for transfer learning SAM (i.e., finetuning decoder only or finetuning all components of SAM).
label: none

sentence: Our results indicated that while finetuning all components of SAM leads to better performance, the gains are still quite limited, and finetuning only the decoder achieves satisfactory performance.
label: none

sentence: We suspect that Polyp-SAM’s performance can be further improved by adjusting mask decoders to output multiple segmentation masks.
label: none

sentence: In addition, since SAM is based on learning visual patterns from user prompts, it becomes a major bottleneck for developing fully end-to-end polyp segmentation models using SAM.
label: none

sentence: While our Polyp-SAMs require ground truth bounding boxes as prompts for optimal performance, we believe that our model still has clinical significance, as manual annotations are time-consuming and tedious for physicians to perform on each image.
label: none

sentence: Given Polyp-SAM's state-of-the-art performance in five public datasets using cross- dataset evaluation, we believe that our model is robust to distribution shifts in various clinical colonoscopy data.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, SAM is an image segmentation model, while the clinical applications for colonoscopy should be video segmentation models.
label: none

sentence: It is im- portant to clarify and distinguish the mission of manifold denoising and a closely related mission of manifold fitting .
label: none

sentence: In the manifold denoising problem, we aim to denoise each sample from the noisy dataset and recover the associated clean sample on the manifold , while in the manifold fitting problem, we aim to recover the man- ifold from the (possibly) noisy dataset.
label: none

sentence: Intuitively, we can denoise the manifold first and fit the manifold by some “interpolation” idea, or we can fit the manifold first and denoise the dataset by projecting the noisy dataset to the clean manifold.

sentence: The manifold fitting problem can be traced back to the work on principle curve and surface [30] and recent development in the principle manifold framework [36].

sentence: HOW SOCIAL REINFORCEMENT LEARNING CAN LEAD TO METASTABLE POLARISATION AND THE VOTER MODEL BV MEYLAHN AND JM MEYLAHN Abstract.
label: none

sentence: Previous explanations for the persistence of polarization of opinions have typically included modelling assumptions that predispose the possibility of polarization (i.e., assumptions allowing a pair of agents to drift apart in their opinion such as repulsive interactions or bounded confidence).
label: none

sentence: An exception is a recent simulation study showing that polarization is persistent when agents form their opinions using social reinforcement learning.
label: none

sentence: Our goal is to highlight the arXiv:2406.07993v2 [physics.soc-ph] 15 Oct 2024 usefulness of reinforcement learning in the context of modeling opinion dynamics, but that caution is required when selecting the tools used to study such a model.
label: none

sentence: We show that the polarization observed in the model of the simulation study cannot persist indefinitely, and exhibits consensus asymptotically with probability one.
label: none

sentence: By constructing a link between the reinforcement learning model and the voter model, we argue that the observed polarization is metastable.
label: none

sentence: Finally, we show that a slight modification in the learning process of the agents changes the model from being non-ergodic to being ergodic.
label: none

sentence: Our results show that reinforcement learning may be a powerful method for modelling polarization in opinion dynamics, but that the tools (objects to study such as the stationary distribution, or time to absorption for example) appropriate for analysing such models crucially depend on their properties (such as ergodicity, or transience).
label: none

sentence: These properties are determined by the details of the learning process and may be difficult to identify based solely on simulations.
label: none

sentence: Since at least 1964 scientists have been trying to answer the question “what on earth must one assume to generate the bimodal outcome of community cleavage studies” [1, p. 153].
label: none

sentence: Possible answers to this question have been presented; bounded confidence [2, 3, 4, 5] whereby agents stop listening to others if their opinion is too different from their own, repulsive forces between agents [6, 7, 8, 9, 10] based on possible negative connections within a network or messages eliciting the opposite effect within a recipient, stubbornness of an agent toward changing their opinion [11, 12, 13], and distinguishing between an agent’s expressed opinion and their internal opinion [14, 15].
label: none

sentence: What unifies these explanations is that the resulting models all include some element from which one might infer the possibility of polarization.
label: none

sentence: Models with only attractive forces on the other hand, typically lead only to consensus (see for example the models of weighted averaging [16, 17, 18, 19] 1 2 BV MEYLAHN AND JM MEYLAHN and imitation [20, 21]).
label: none

sentence: Thus it comes as a surprise that the model studied by Banisch and Olbrich [22] with only attractive forces between agents, seems to exhibit persistent polarization.
label: none

sentence: The dynamics in models of opinion formation typically take place on a network.
label: none

sentence: A network consists of nodes (representing agents) and edges between them (representing social influence or ties).
label: none

sentence: Nodes that share an edge are said to be neighbours in the network.
label: none

sentence: A well studied class of opinion dynamics models on networks from the sociophysics literature is the class of voter models [20, 21] (see [23] for an introduction).
label: none

sentence: In these models a random agent is selected each round to update their opinion.
label: none

sentence: The agent does this by copying the opinion held by one of their neighbours.
label: none

sentence: Reinforcement learning is a model for learning by feedback: actions (or opinions in our case) for which an agent receives positive feedback are reinforced.
label: none

sentence: Actions that receive negative feedback on the other hand are less likely to be taken in the future.
label: none

sentence: For convenience, in the remainder we refer to the paper of Banisch and Olbrich [22] as BO while we refer to the reinforcement learning model they study as the ‘Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning for Opinion Dynamics model,’ or simply the ARLOD model.
label: none

sentence: This influential model includes no repulsive element in the interaction between agents.
label: none

sentence: It proposes modelling the evolution of opinions (of agents on connected networks) using multiagent reinforcement learning, where agents interact via a coordination game.
label: none

sentence: They find, using simulations, that allowing agents to learn their opinion through trial and error gives rise to the emergence of persistent 1 polarization.
label: none

sentence: This is surprising, because in this model after an interaction between two agents, the opinions of the two necessarily get closer together and cannot remain unchanged or get further apart.
label: none

sentence: That is, in the ARLOD model there are no repulsive forces or assumptions of bounded confidence 2 .
label: none

sentence: T¨ornberg et al. [25] build on the ideas of the ARLOD model by incorporating the role of agent identity.
label: none

sentence: T¨ornberg [26], similarly looking for drivers of polarisation without the assumption of negative influences but dissatisfied with BO’s assumption of selective exposure (a fixed and constant network), analysed a model which includes non-local interaction to model the effect of media.
label: none

sentence: A variant of the reinforcement learning model with multiple opinions and synchronous updating has been studied in [27].
label: none

sentence: Their results highlight the difficulty of reaching consensus in complex networks using reinforcement learning.
label: none

sentence: The idea of modelling opinion dynamics by reinforcement learning has been built on since (e.g. [28, 29, 30, 31]).
label: none

sentence: An overarching goal in this paper is to highlight the importance of the relationship between model assumptions and characteristics.
label: none

sentence: It can be tempting to design a model and study its characteristics by simulation.
label: none

sentence: However, to accurately present the results of such a simulation study it may be important to first identify certain model characteristics.
label: none

sentence: We illustrate the importance of this by presenting three results on the ARLOD model by BO [22].
label: none

sentence: We show analytically that consensus is reached in the ARLOD model with probability one in the long run.
label: none

sentence: The polarisation found in [22] necessarily gives way to consensus eventually.
label: none

sentence: To elucidate this result, we run simulations to estimate the tail probabilities for the time to consensus.
label: none

sentence: We find that these exhibit heavy tails, indicating that there may be metastable states (corresponding to polarization) in which the model resides for a long time before reaching consensus.
label: none

sentence: The phenomenon of metastable polarization together with eventual consensus has previously been observed in the context of the voter model, first introduced in [21].
label: none

sentence: Specifically, consensus is reached eventually if the state space of the model is finite [32], and it has been shown that polarisation is metastable in certain network topologies [33, 34, 35, 36].
label: none

sentence: Recently, metastable opinion polarisation has been identified in [37] where it is shown to arise from biased information processing.
label: none

sentence: The dynamics of the voter model on networks consists of agents adopting one of their neighbours’ opinions at random.
label: none

sentence: At first sight, dynamics of this kind seem rudimentary in comparison to the sophisticated dynamics of reinforcement learning.
label: none

sentence: However, we show that, under a separation 1 In the original article BO [22], ‘persistent’ and ‘stable’ are used interchangeably.
label: none

sentence: In order to avoid confusion, we use ‘persistent’ to discuss their claims about the ARLOD model and ‘stable’ when making our own claims. 2 Models of opinion dynamics may be classified into ‘assimilative,’ ‘repulsive’ and models with ‘similarity bias’ [24].
label: none

sentence: The model under consideration here does not traditionally fall in the category of models with only assimilative forces between agents because it utilizes experience based learning.
label: none

sentence: SOCIAL REINFORCEMENT LEARNING 3 of time scales, the ARLOD model converges in distribution to a voter model.
label: none

sentence: This relationship highlights that the polarisation observed in the ARLOD model may indeed be metastable depending on the network structure.
label: none

sentence: It also bridges the seemingly disparate approaches to modelling opinions: sociophysics and computational sociology.
label: none

sentence: These two approaches differ in their typical level of abstraction, and whether they aim for tractability by keeping the dynamics simple or aim to approach realism by modelling the agents with a relatively high level of sophistication.
label: none

sentence: The ARLOD model falls in the class of computational sociology seeing as the agents in the model are sophisticated enough to learn from experience.
label: none

sentence: The relationship we show between this model and the voter model (a very simple model where agents imitate one another) is thus an example of a bridge between the two approaches to studying polarization.
label: none

sentence: In designing their model, BO [22] decide to make the interaction-learning relationship asymmetric: only one of the agents partaking in the interaction is allowed to explore and learn from the expe- rience.
label: none

sentence: We show that adapting the model to be symmetric fundamentally changes the nature of the opinion dynamics from being non-ergodic to being ergodic.
label: none

sentence: Under this model, consensus is no longer absorbing so that the tools appropriate for studying polarization and consensus differ from those required in the case of the ARLOD model.
label: none

sentence: For example, in an ergodic system the stationary distribution may be estimated by studying the mean return time to polarized (or consensus) states.
label: none

sentence: On the other hand for a non-ergodic system with absorbing states one typically studies the time to absorption (in a consensus or polarized state if these are indeed absorbing) or the number of visits to transient states before absorption.
label: none

sentence: If there are both consensus and polarized absorbing states, the relative probability of consensus or polarization can be studied. 2.

sentence: To assess the condition and performance of structures, various methodologies have been proposed to update the parameters of dynamic analysis models using monitoring data.
label: none

sentence: The dynamic analysis model that is originally based on assumptions made during the design phase requires adjustments to incorporate monitoring data.
label: none

sentence: These adjustments are crucial for assessing the performance of structures during their lifetimes.
label: none

sentence: Nevertheless, monitoring data, such as vibration responses, often lacks sufficient information on the parameters of dynamic analysis models [1], [2].
label: none

sentence: For instance, vibrational responses during minor earthquakes may not provide information regarding parameters related to nonlinear responses.
label: none

sentence: Additionally, acceleration monitoring at floor level does not provide direct ©2024.
label: none

sentence: This manuscript version is made available under the CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 license https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ information on damage to structural or nonstructural members.
label: none

sentence: The limited information from monitoring data introduces uncertainty into the estimation of the model parameters.
label: none

sentence: Consequently, structural model-updating techniques should account for this lack of information and the associated uncertainties in the estimated model parameters.
label: none

sentence: Such uncertainty can be described through the probability distribution of model parameters or by using a family of plausible model parameters that have been numerically estimated, instead of searching for the best estimate [3], [4], [5].
label: none

sentence: The performance of structures can be effectively assessed without bias [6], [7] by obtaining the probability distribution of the model parameters for a dynamic analysis model that incorporates these uncertainties.
label: none

sentence: Thus, the Bayesian approach is effective for this purpose.
label: none

sentence: Within the realm of the Bayesian approach, modal-based approaches for Bayesian model updating have been developed [8], [9], [10], [11].
label: none

sentence: These methods utilize modal parameters, such as modal frequencies and mode shapes, which are estimated from the observed structural responses for model updating.
label: none

sentence: Time-domain approaches [12], [13], [14], which are suitable for situations in which the structural properties vary over time, and frequency-domain approaches [15], [16], in which both the input and output need to be measured, have also been proposed.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, methods incorporating machine learning techniques within the Bayesian updating framework, such as the active learning of kriging [17], a pattern-recognition method [18], and the Bayesian inference approach [19], have been proposed.
label: none

sentence: However, these methods frequently involve approximations and simplifications, primarily because of their theoretical limitations.
label: none

sentence: This is particularly true when high-dimensional and correlated observations, such as time- or frequency-domain data, are applied to Bayesian structural model updating [20], [21].
label: none

sentence: To approximate the posterior distribution of the model parameters specifically in this context, an approximate Bayesian computation was developed [22], [23], [24].
label: none

sentence: In this study, a multimodal VAE [25], [26], [27] was employed to develop a versatile framework for Bayesian structural model updating.
label: none

sentence: A multimodal VAE is an enhanced version of the original VAE [28] and is a notable tool in the field of machine learning.
label: none

sentence: The proposed methodology provides a robust means of model updating for various structural models and measurements, effectively addressing uncertainties in the updated model parameters.
label: none

sentence: In the proposed approach, which utilizes a multimodal VAE, the computational demands are significantly lower than that of the original VAE, while the accuracy required for practical applications is maintained.
label: none
