sentence: Spiking neural networks (SNNs), inspired from neuroscience, are a positive step in the direction of achieving the required energy efficiency.
label: none

sentence: However, in a bid to lower the energy requirements, accuracy is marginally sacrificed.
label: none

sentence: Hence, predictions of such deep learning algorithms require an uncertainty measure that can inform users regarding the bounds of a cer- tain output.
label: none

sentence: In this paper, we introduce the Conformalized Randomized Prior Operator (CRP-O) framework that leverages Randomized Prior (RP) networks and Split Conformal Prediction (SCP) to quantify uncertainty in both conventional and spiking neural operators.
label: none

sentence: To further enable zero- shot super-resolution in UQ, we propose an extension incorporating Gaussian Process Regression.
label: none

sentence: This enhanced super-resolution-enabled CRP-O framework is integrated with the recently developed Variable Spiking Wavelet Neural Operator (VSWNO).
label: none

sentence: To test the performance of the obtained cal- ibrated uncertainty bounds, we discuss four different examples covering both one-dimensional and two-dimensional partial differential equations.
label: none

sentence: Results demonstrate that the uncertainty bounds pro- duced by the conformalized RP-VSWNO significantly enhance UQ estimates compared to vanilla RP-VSWNO, Quantile WNO (Q-WNO), and Conformalized Quantile WNO (CQ-WNO).
label: none

sentence: These findings underscore the potential of the proposed approach for practical applications.

sentence: K eywords Variable Spiking Neuron · Operator learning · Wavelet Neural Operator · Spiking Neurons · Uncertainty Quantification 1 Introduction Machine learning [1–3] in the current day and age has crossed the initiation threshold and has steamrolled its way into various aspects of science and engineering [4–14].
label: none

sentence: The increasing appearance of the term scientific machine learning in literature [15–17] is a testament to the same.
label: none

sentence: A huge chunk of this credit goes to the rapid development of neural network [18–20] algorithms, which have shown tremendous performance across various scientific tasks.
label: none

sentence: Developments like operator learning algorithms [21–24] have made it relatively easier to learn datasets originating from complex partial differential equations, which are often used to model the physical space around us, whether natural or artificial.
label: none

sentence: However, despite the ongoing improvements, their performance is not at par with the gold standard techniques like finite element modeling [25,26].
label: none

sentence: This is further true for spiking variants of these operator learning algorithms [27,28], a domain that is particularly important from the view of a sustainable future and edge computing.
label: none

sentence: Naturally, a confidence measure that can inform the user as to how reliable a specific output is and what its boundaries/extremes are becomes essential.
label: none

sentence: Such measures can prove instrumental in tasks where some form of decision-making is involved.
label: none

sentence: A PREPRINT - D ECEMBER 13, 2024 Uncertainty associated with the predictions/outputs of an underlying model is usually represented in the form of confidence intervals or uncertainty bounds.
label: none

sentence: These bounds can give Conditional Coverage (CC) or Marginal CC (MCC) [29, 30] depending on the algorithm adopted for Uncertainty Quantification (UQ).
label: none

sentence: To understand this, assume that we have a set of inputs with n samples, and we have uncertainty bounds corresponding to each sample.
label: none

sentence: Then CC s implies that for all samples individually, the probability that the corresponding true value will lie within their stipulated bounds is ≥ 1 − α , α ∈ (0 , 1) being the miscoverage level or error rate.
label: none

sentence: MCC, on the other hand, is applicable to the whole population and states that among all n samples’s true values, ≥ n (1 − α ) true values should lie between s s their uncertainty bounds.
label: none

sentence: Although CC is more powerful than MCC, getting bounds that satisfy CC within neural network algorithms is non-trivial [31, 32].
label: none

sentence: Therefore, the focus is often on developing algorithms that yield MCC.
label: none

sentence: Unfortunately, this is often rendered ineffective because of the inherent assumptions associated with the algorithms.
label: none

sentence: For example, in Bayesian approaches for UQ [33–35], we often assume some prior distribution and make assumptions about the noise present in the system.
label: none

sentence: In frequentist ensemble approaches as well, in order to report bounds that give coverage with probability ≥ 1 − α , we have to take the Gaussian assumption.
label: none

sentence: Such assumptions, coupled with imperfect optimization of the underlying model, lead to imperfect uncertainty bounds.
label: none

sentence: To tackle this challenge, researchers use UQ techniques like Conformal Prediction [29, 30, 36] (CP).
label: none

sentence: CP is a distribution-free UQ technique that provides bounds that satisfy MCC conditions without the underlying strong as- sumptions, as in the case of Bayesian approaches.
label: none

sentence: In this paper, we propose a Conformalized Randomized Prior Operator (CRP-O) framework for UQ.
label: none

sentence: The proposed framework utilizes the concept of Randomized Prior (RP) net- works [37] and extends it to a base neural operator in order to arrive at a heuristic measure of uncertainty.
label: none

sentence: This initial estimate is then calibrated using Split CP [29,30,36] to get the desired coverage using the estimated uncertainty and, hence, to satisfy the MCC condition.
label: none

sentence: The motivation for adopting the RP networks to arrive at an initial heuristic estimate of uncertainty is that while being set in a deterministic framework, it also allows users to incorporate any prior information regarding the dataset, and it is trivial to implement even for complex architectures.
label: none

sentence: We have further enhanced the CRP-O framework by exploiting a Gaussian Process to enable zero-shot super-resolution in UQ The proposed enhanced CRP-O framework is used in conjunction with the Variable Spiking Wavelet Neural Operator [27] (VSWNO), which is a spiking variant of vanilla Wavelet Neural Operator [23] (WNO) architecture.
label: none

sentence: The applicability of the CRP-O framework is also shown when vanilla WNO is used as the base operator.
label: none

sentence: We note that there are two prior work that have proposed conformal prediction in neural operator.
label: none

sentence: Moya et al. [31] proposed a UQ technique for Deep Operator Network [21] (DeepONet) architecture using SCP, and it proposes the use of quantile regression for training the base operator.
label: none

sentence: Ma et al. [32] proposed Risk-Controlling Quantile Neural Operator (RCQNO) thar relies on quntile regression for obtaining the initial uncertainty estimates and couples it with SCP.
label: none

sentence: However, quantile regression often suffer from crossing quantiles, that can reduce the effectiveness of SCP.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, (RCQNO) [32] requires splitting the available datasets into three different parts, which can be problematic for applications with limited data.
label: none

sentence: Four examples are discussed to test the efficacy of the proposed approach, and we compare the coverage of uncertainty bounds obtained using the CRP-VSWNO/ CRP-WNO with those obtained using vanilla RP-VSWNO/ RP-WNO [38], Q-WNO, and conformalized Q-WNO (CQ-WNO).
label: none

sentence: The results produced show that while the latter fails to satisfy the MCC condition, the former gives the required coverage for the test dataset when analyzed as a whole.
label: none

sentence: A comparison of the performance of conformalized RP-WNO is also drawn against the performance of RCQNO.
label: none

sentence: The highlights of the proposed framework include, • Application to VSWNO : In this paper, we show the applicability of the proposed framework to VSWNO.
label: none

sentence: Spiking neural networks promise a more energy-efficient approach to deep learning, but because of their inherent sparse communication, the accuracy achieved is slightly affected.
label: none

sentence: Thus, it becomes important to quantify the uncertainty associated with their predictions, and the proposed framework is able to capture the same effectively. • RP-Operator as the heuristic measure of uncertainty : RP-Operator as an initial uncertainty estimator has the advantage of being set in a deterministic framework, which allows users to implement it for complex datasets easily.
label: none

sentence: It can also incorporate prior information regarding the dataset, which is often omitted in a deterministic framework.
label: none

sentence: It should be noted that despite its trivial nature, the underlying uncertainty estimates are robust enough that with the help of a meager calibration dataset, they can be improved to provide better coverage, and its mean predictions give a good approximation of the ground truth. • Limited data split : The proposed framework requires the original dataset to be split into only two parts, (i) the training dataset and (ii) the calibration dataset.
label: none

sentence: This is helpful in cases where the dataset available is sparse and limited. 2 A PREPRINT - D ECEMBER 13, 2024 • Super-resolution predictions : In this paper, using the Gaussian process [39,40], we show how the proposed framework can be extended for uncertainty quantification in super-resolution predictions of RP operator net- works.
label: none

label: none

sentence: Specifically, the continuous activations σ ( · ) of artificial neurons used in vanilla WNO architecture are replaced by Variable Spiking Neurons [43] (VSNs), giving rise to sparse communication and hence energy efficiency.

sentence: The incorporation of prior information can also take the form of known physics or domain-specific constraints.

sentence: This ensemble-based approach not only enhances robustness but also facilitates seamless integration of domain knowledge into the learning process, making RP networks a powerful tool for uncertainty-aware predictions.

sentence: To address this, we propose in this paper, a distribution free uncertainty quantification framework in neu- roscience inspired spiking operators.
label: none

sentence: The proposed framework uses the uncertainty bounds from randomized prior (RP) operators as its initial uncertainty estimates and calibrates them using the split conformal prediction (SCP) algo- rithm to provide the required coverage.
label: none

sentence: The selection of the RP operator for obtaining the initial estimate of uncertainty is based on the hypothesis that a good initial estimate will improve the SCP algorithm’s calibration performance.
label: none

sentence: It is also based on the fact that the RP operators are easily scalable to complex architectures, are computationally efficient, and can account for prior information while being set in a deterministic framework.
label: none

sentence: Super-resolution is a defining property for operator learning algorithms, and gauging uncertainty associated with super-resolution predictions is important because, in this case, the trained model is predicting at solution grid locations that are unseen during training.
label: none

sentence: In response to this challenge, we also enhance the algorithm to allow uncertainty quantification in zero-shot super-resolution setup.
label: none

sentence: The developed algorithm is integrated with the recently developed variable spiking wavelet neural operator (VSWNO) and the vanilla wavelet neural operator (WNO) so as to enable uncertainty quantification in these operators.
label: none

sentence: False Positive Reduction by Actively Mining Negative Samples for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in Chest Radiographs arXiv:1807.10756v1 [cs.CV] 26 Jul 2018 Sejin Park ∗ Woochan Hwang Kyu Hwan Jung VUNO Inc.

sentence: Seoul, South Korea Imperial College London Seoul, South Korea UK Joon Beom Seo Namkug Kim Asan Medical Center Asan Medical Center University of Ulsan University of Ulsan Seoul, South Korea Seoul, South Korea Abstract Generating large quantities of quality labeled data in medical imaging is very time consuming and expensive.
label: none

sentence: The performance of supervised algorithms for various tasks on imaging has improved drastically over the years, however the availability of data to train these algorithms have become one of the main bottlenecks for implementation.
label: none

sentence: To address this, we propose a semi-supervised learning method where pseudo-negative labels from unlabeled data are used to further reﬁne the performance of a pulmonary nodule detection network in chest radiographs.
label: none

sentence: After training with the proposed network, the false positive rate was reduced to 0.1266 from 0.4864 while maintaining sensitivity at 0.89.
label: none

sentence: K eywords Convolutional neural network · Lung nodule detection · False positive reduction · Negative sample mining · Semantic segmentation 1 Introduction For many medical images, labeled data (with lesion labels) can be in short supply.
label: none

sentence: However, unlabeled data (with unknown lesion and class labels) tends to be more readily available.
label: none

sentence: This has been a major limiting factor in applying machine learning to medical imaging.
label: none

sentence: To tackle this problem, we propose a novel semi supervised learning method for lung nodule detection in chest radiographs.
label: none

sentence: While CAD (Computer aided detection) systems can achieve high sensitivity, their relatively low speciﬁcity has limited its implementation in the clinical setting.
label: none

sentence: Most CAD systems therefore, utilize various false positive reduction methods to improve system speciﬁcity.
label: none

sentence: Our approach here is to use semi-supervised learning, which allows us to use the pseudo-negative labeled data hidden amongst the unlabeled data.
label: none

sentence: The goal of this study is to develop a method that allows us to use the pseudo-negative labeled data via transfer learning to improve performance of the detection task.
label: none

sentence: We also showed that using clinically ∗ Corresponding author: gnoses@gmail.com veriﬁed negative data improves speciﬁcity.
label: none

sentence: On the other hand, we found that the inclusion of whole unlabeled data, which has both positive and negative data, degrades the sensitivity score. 2 Methods We used chest radiographs (PA view) collected from 2013 to 2015 at Asan Medical Center.
label: none

sentence: There were 1970 labeled radiographs, where suspicious lung nodules were marked by clinicians on the images as regions of interest.
label: none

sentence: We also had 3000 unlabeled chest radiographs, which were used during the second phase of our proposed method.
label: none

sentence: In addition, we used 3000 clinically veriﬁed normal radiographs to validate our hypothesis that using additional negative data will improve the false positive rate.
label: none

sentence: The 1970 radiographs used for this study were anonymized and reviewed by the internal review board at Asan Medical Centre before being provided to us.
label: none

sentence: During the pre-processing stage, we used per image histogram equalization to mitigate the variance of intensity amongst the radiographs.
label: none

sentence: In our model, data augmentation (rotation, random crop, resize, intensity and contrast noise) had no signiﬁcant effect in terms of training and validation accuracy.
label: none

sentence: Therefore, we did not apply any augmentations to our data as they increased the training time with no signiﬁcant beneﬁt.
label: none

sentence: Our proposed method is a two phase learning model.
label: none

sentence: In the ﬁrst phase, we used the pixel labeled data from 1970 labeled radiographs to train a U-net [1] like encoder decoder network for semantic segmentation.
label: none

sentence: To handle small sized nodules, a class balanced loss function was used.
label: none

sentence: The U-net like lateral/skip connection from lower layers to higher layers performs well on small datasets of medical images.
label: none

sentence: Then we added inception modules in several layers of the encoder part which made our network 30% faster without degradation of accuracy.
label: none

sentence: We trained our model for 20 hours using the ADAM [2] optimizer in Tensorﬂow.
label: none

sentence: For the ﬁrst phase, we conﬁrmed our best FROC score from the 1970 labeled data via 5 folds cross validation.
label: none

sentence: The 1970 cases were divided into 5 subsets of similar size.
label: none

sentence: For each fold, 4 subsets were used for training and 1 subset was used for validation and testing.
label: none

sentence: Figure 1: Training procedure and network architecture of proposed method During the second phase, we used the trained network from the ﬁrst phase to discover pseudo-negative samples from prediction results of the 3000 unlabeled data.
label: none

sentence: If no nodules were detected from the prediction, the samples were considered pseudo-negative samples.
label: none

sentence: We discarded any other unlabeled data.
label: none

sentence: Both labeled and reﬁned pseudo negative samples were then used jointly to train our model.
label: none

sentence: The network in the second phase had transferred weights from the whole layers of the ﬁrst phase network.
label: none

sentence: The network architecture and the test set of the ﬁrst and second phase is identical. 2 3 Results The proposed ‘Negative sample reﬁning method’ attained a performance of 0.1266 false positives per scan.
label: none

sentence: Our results show that using reﬁned pseudo-negative data can decrease the number of false positives per scan by 73% while maintaining sensitivity.
label: none

sentence: As seen in Table 1, FROC of the ﬁrst phase was 0.8924 and 0.4864 for sensitivity and false positives per scan, respectively.
label: none

sentence: After the second phase, the false positive rate is improved to 0.1266, while maintaining baseline sensitivity at 0.889, which is superior to previous studies.
label: none

sentence: In the ﬁgure, we can observe that the false positive lesion detected after the ﬁrst phase (b) disappears after the second phase (c).
label: none

sentence: Figure 2: Illustration of result by proposed method (a) gold standard (b) ﬁrst phase (c) second phase In order to prove that discovering true negative samples from unlabeled data is an effective approach to false positive reduction, we experimented by using clinically veriﬁed negative data.
label: none

sentence: As seen in Table 2, the sensitivity was maintained at 0.89, while the false positive rate decreased to 0.0827.
label: none

sentence: These results support the hypothesis which led to the development of our semi supervised learning method.
label: none

sentence: Table 2: Comparison of FROC performance in 3 data sources.
label: none

sentence: Approved : clinically approved true negative data.
label: none

sentence: Pseudo negative : reﬁned pseudo negative data.
label: none

sentence: In Table 2, the sensitivity of 0.8924 after the ﬁrst phase decreases to 0.853 after the second phase training with unreﬁned unlabeled data. 4 Discussion Through this study, we showed that signiﬁcant improvement in the false positive rate can be achieved by our proposed method.
label: none

sentence: We conﬁrmed that clinically veriﬁed true negatives are effective in reducing the false positive rate, and the fact that the resulting false positive rate is similar to what we achieved with reﬁned pseudo-negative data shows the potential of this method.
label: none

sentence: Nonetheless, the given task is detecting nodules not all abnormal lesions, and because the data used for phase 1 training were not labeled for non-nodular lesions to start with, the pseudo negative data found by our method is not meaningless.
label: none

sentence: Also, since the experimental results show improvement of the FROC deﬁned for a given problem, the proposed method can be claimed to be effective. 5 Conclusion We proposed a novel semi supervised learning method for false positive reduction of the nodule detection task in chest radiographs.
label: none

sentence: Supervised tensor decomposition with features on multiple modes Jiaxin Hu, Chanwoo Lee, and Miaoyan Wang ∗ Department of Statistics, University of Wisconsin-Madison arXiv:1910.09499v2 [stat.ME] 18 Aug 2021 Abstract Higher-order tensors have received increased attention across science and engineer- ing.
label: none

sentence: While most tensor decomposition methods are developed for a single tensor ob- servation, scientiﬁc studies often collect side information, in the form of node features and interactions thereof, together with the tensor data.
label: none

sentence: Such data problems are com- mon in neuroimaging, network analysis, and spatial-temporal modeling.
label: none

sentence: Identifying the relationship between a high-dimensional tensor and side information is important yet challenging.
label: none

sentence: Here, we develop a tensor decomposition method that incorporates mul- tiple feature matrices as side information.
label: none

sentence: Unlike unsupervised tensor decomposition, our supervised decomposition captures the eﬀective dimension reduction of the data tensor conﬁned to feature space of interest.
label: none

sentence: An eﬃcient alternating optimization algo- rithm with provable spectral initialization is further developed.
label: none

sentence: Our proposal handles a broad range of data types, including continuous, count, and binary observations.
label: none

sentence: We apply the method to diﬀusion tensor imaging data from human connectome project and multi-relational political network data.
label: none

sentence: We identify the key global connectivity pattern and pinpoint the local regions that are associated with available features.
label: none

sentence: Our simu- lation code, R-package , and datasets used in the paper are available tensorregress at https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tensorregress .
label: none

sentence: Keywords: Tensor data analysis, Supervised dimension reduction, Exponential family dis- tribution, Generalized multilinear model, Alternating optimization ∗ The authors gratefully acknowledge NSF grant DMS-1915978 and funding from the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation.
label: none

sentence: Corresponding author: Miaoyan Wang, miaoyan.wang@wisc.edu. 1 1 Introduction Multi-dimensional arrays, known as tensors, are often collected with side information on multiple modes in modern scientiﬁc and engineering studies.
label: none

sentence: A popular example is in neuroimaging ( Zhou et al. , 2013 ).
label: none

sentence: The brain connectivity networks are collected from a sample of individuals, accompanied by individual characteristics such as age, gender, and diseases status (see Figure 1 a).
label: none

sentence: Another example is in network analysis ( Berthet and Baldin , 2020 ; Hoﬀ , 2005 ).
label: none

sentence: A typical social network consists of nodes that represent people and edges that represent friendships.
label: none

sentence: Side information such as people’s demographic information and friendship types are often available.
label: none

sentence: In both examples, we are interested in identifying the variation in the data tensor (e.g., brain connectivities, social community patterns) that is aﬀected by available features.
label: none

sentence: These seemingly diﬀerent scenarios pose a common yet challenging problem for tensor data modeling.
label: none

sentence: In addition to the aforementioned challenges, many tensor datasets consist of non- Gaussian measurements.
label: none

sentence: Examples include the political interaction dataset ( Nickel et al. , 2011 ) which measures action counts between countries under various relations, and the brain connectivity network dataset ( Zhou et al. , 2013 ; Wang and Li , 2020 ) which is a col- lection of binary adjacency matrices.
label: none

sentence: Classical tensor decomposition methods are based on minimizing the Frobenius norm of deviation, leading to suboptimal predictions for binary- or count-valued response variables.
label: none

sentence: A number of supervised tensor methods have been pro- posed ( Lock and Li , 2018 ; Li and Zhang , 2017 ; Sun and Li , 2017 ; Hao et al. , 2021 ; Raskutti et al. , 2019 ) to address the tensor regression problem in various forms, such as scalar-to- tensor regression and tensor-response regression.
label: none

sentence: These methods often assume Gaussian distribution for the tensor entries, or impose random designs for the feature matrices, both of which are less suitable for applications of our interest.
label: none

sentence: The gap between theory and practice means a great opportunity to model paradigms and better capture the complexity in tensor data.
label: none

sentence: We present a general model and associated method for decomposing a data tensor whose entries are from exponential family with side information.
label: none

sentence: We formulate the learning task as a structured regression problem, with tensor observation serving as the response, and the multiple side information as features.
label: none

sentence: Figure 1 b illustrates our model in the special 2 Figure 1: Examples of supervised tensor decomposition with side information.
label: none

sentence: (b) Spatio-temporal growth model. case of order-3 tensors.
label: none

sentence: A low-rank structure is imposed to the conditional mean of tensor R d × r observation, where unlike classical decomposition, the tensor factors X M ∈ k k be- k k R d × p long to the space spanned by features X ∈ k k for k = 1 , 2 , 3.
label: none

sentence: The unknown matrices k R p × r M ∈ k k (referred to as “dimension reduction matrices”) link the conditional mean k to the feature spaces, thereby allowing the identiﬁcation of variations in the tensor data attributable to the side information.
label: none

sentence: Our proposal blends the modeling power of generalized linear model (GLM) and the exploratory capability of tensor dimension reduction in order to take the best out of both worlds.
label: none

sentence: We leverage GLM to allow heteroscedacity due to the mean-variance relationship in the non-Gaussian data.
label: none

sentence: This ﬂexibility is important in practice.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, our low-rank model on the (transformed) conditional mean tensor eﬀectively mitigates the curse of high dimensionality.
label: none

sentence: In classical GLM, the sample size and feature dimension are well deﬁned; however, in the tensor data analysis, we observe only one realization of an order- K tensor and up to K feature matrices.
label: none

sentence: Both the number of tensor entries and feature dimension grow exponentially in K .
label: none

sentence: Dimension reduction is therefore crucial for prediction and interpretability.
label: none

sentence: We establish the statistical and algorithmic convergences of our estimator, and we quantify the gain in accuracy through simulations and case studies.
label: none

sentence: Our work is closely related to but also clearly distinctive from several lines of previous work.
label: none

sentence: The ﬁrst line is a class of unsupervised tensor decomposition such as classical Tucker and CP decomposition ( De Lathauwer et al. , 2000 ; Kolda and Bader , 2009 ) and generalized decomposition for non-Gaussian data ( Chi and Kolda , 2012 ; Tarzanagh and Michailidis , 2019 ; Hong et al. , 2020 ; Li , 2020 ).
label: none

sentence: Regardless of the implementation, the unsupervised 3 methods aim to ﬁnd the best low-rank representation of a data tensor alone.
label: none

sentence: In contrast, our model is a supervised tensor learning, which aims to identify the association between a data tensor and multiple features.
label: none

sentence: The low-rank factorization is determined jointly by the tensor data and feature matrices in our model.
label: none

sentence: The second line of work studies the tensor-to-tensor regression.
label: none

sentence: As we show in Section 5 , our supervised tensor decomposition falls into this general category, and we provide a provable solution in new settings that have broader practical signiﬁcance.
label: none

sentence: Earlier work in this vein ( Lock , 2018 ; Lock and Li , 2018 ; Gahrooei et al. , 2020 ; Li , 2020 ) focuses on algorithm development, but not on the statistical accuracy.
label: none

sentence: Li and Zhang ( 2017 ) introduces an envelope-based approach to identify suﬃcient dimension reduction ( Adragni and Cook , 2009 ), but its theory is restricted to Gaussian data with one-sided feature matrix only.
label: none

sentence: Raskutti et al. ( 2019 ) establishes the statistical accuracy for convex relaxed maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) of tensor regression.
label: none

sentence: However, convex relaxation for tensor optimizations suﬀers from computational intractability and statistical sub-optimality.
label: none

sentence: Recent work has demonstrated the success of non-convex approaches in various tensor problems ( Sun and Li , 2017 ; Zhang et al. , 2018 ; Raskutti et al. , 2019 ; Han et al. , 2020 ); we go step further by allowing multiple feature matrices with either ﬁxed or random designs.
label: none

sentence: In Sections 4.2 , we show that incorporating multiple feature matrices substantially improves the statistical accuracy.
label: none

sentence: A.3 Comparison with GLMs under stochastic block models We investigate the performance of our model under correlated feature eﬀects.

label: none

sentence: These features may represent, for example, age, gender, cognitive score, etc. Recent study has suggested that brain connectivity networks often exhibit community structure represented as a collection of subnetworks, and each subnetwork is comprised of a set of spatially distributed brain nodes.
label: none

sentence: To accommodate this structure, we utilize the stochastic block model ( Abbe , 2017 ) to generate the eﬀect size.
label: none

sentence: Speciﬁcally, we partition the nodes into r blocks by assigning each node to a block with uniform probability.
label: none

sentence: Edges within a same block are assumed to share the same feature eﬀects, where the eﬀects are i.i.d. drawn from N (0 , 1).
label: none

sentence: We then apply our tensor regression model to the network data using the BIC-selected rank.

sentence: A typical RTB setup consists of pub- lishers, supply-side platforms (SSP), data management platforms (DMP), ad exchange (ADX), and demand-side platforms (DSP).
label: none

sentence: When an online browsing activity triggers an ad request in one bidding round, the SSP sends this request to the DSP through the ADX, where eligible ads compete for the impression.
label: none

sentence: The bidding agent, DSP, repre- sents advertisers to come up with an optimal bid and transmits the bid back to the ADX (e.g., usually within less than 100ms [23]), where the winner is selected to be displayed and charged by a generalized second price (GSP).
label: none

sentence: In the RTB system, bidding optimization in DSP is regarded as the most critical problem [24].
label: none

sentence: Thus, our work focuses on DSP, where bidding optimization happens.
label: none

sentence: In real-time bidding, two fundamental challenges need to be addressed.
label: none

sentence: Firstly, the RTB environ- ment is highly dynamic.
label: none

sentence: In [20,24,26], researchers make a strong assumption that the bidding process is stationary over time.
label: none

sentence: However, the sequence of user queries (e.g., incurring impressions, clicks, or conversions) is time-dependent and mostly unpre- dictable [25], where the outcome inﬂuences the next auction round.
label: none

sentence: Traditional al- gorithms usually learn an independent predictor and conduct ﬁxed optimization that amounts to a greedy strategy, often not leading to the optimal return [3].
label: none

sentence: Agents with re- inforcement learning (RL) address the aforementioned challenge to some extent [7,12,25].
label: none

sentence: RL-based methods can alleviate the instability by learning from immediate feedback and long-term reward.
label: none

sentence: However, these methods are limited to either Revenue or ROI , which is only one part of the overall utility.
label: none

sentence: In the problem of RTB, we assume that the utility is two-fold, as outlined: (i) the cumulative cost should be kept within the bud- get; (ii) the overall revenue should be maximized.
label: none

sentence: Therefore, the second challenge is that the real-world RTB industry needs to consider multiple objectives, which are not adequately addressed in the existing literature.
label: none

sentence: To address the challenges mentioned above, we propose a Multi-Objective Actor- Critic model, named MoTiAC .
label: none

sentence: We generalize the popular asynchronous advantage actor-critic (A3C) [13] reinforcement learning algorithm for multiple objectives in the RTB setting.
label: none

sentence: Our model employs several local actor-critic networks with different ob- jectives to interact with the same environment and then updates the global network asynchronously according to different reward signals.
label: none

sentence: Instead of using a ﬁxed linear combination of different objectives, MoTiAC can decide on adaptive weights over time according to how well the current situation conforms with the agent’s prior.
label: none

sentence: We evaluate our model on click data collected from the Tencent ad bidding system.
label: none

sentence: The experimental results verify the effectiveness of our approach versus a set of baselines.
label: none

sentence: The contributions in this paper can be summarized as follows: – We identify two critical challenges in RTB and are well motivated to use multi- objective RL as the solution. – We propose a novel multi-objective actor-critic model MoTiAC for optimal bidding and prove the superiority of our model from the perspective of Pareto optimality.

sentence: Extracting COVID-19 Diagnoses and Symptoms From Clinical Text: A New Annotated Corpus and Neural Event Extraction Framework Kevin Lybarger a, ∗ , Mari Ostendorf b , Matthew Thompson c , Meliha Yetisgen a a Biomedical & Health Informatics, University of Washington, Box 358047, Seattle, WA 98109, USA b Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Washington, Campus Box 352500 185, Seattle, WA 98195-2500, USA c Department of Family Medicine, University of Washington, Box 354696, Seattle, WA 98195-2500, USA arXiv:2012.00974v2 [cs.CL] 10 Mar 2021 Abstract Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a global pandemic.
label: none

sentence: Although much has been learned about the novel coronavirus since its emergence, there are many open questions related to tracking its spread, describing symptomology, predicting the severity of infection, and forecasting healthcare utilization.
label: none

sentence: Free-text clinical notes contain critical information for resolving these questions.
label: none

sentence: Data-driven, automatic information extraction models are needed to use this text-encoded information in large-scale studies.
label: none

sentence: This work presents a new clinical corpus, referred to as the COVID-19 Annotated Clinical Text (CACT) Corpus, which comprises 1,472 notes with detailed annotations characterizing COVID-19 diagnoses, testing, and clinical presentation.
label: none

sentence: We introduce a span-based event extraction model that jointly extracts all annotated phenomena, achieving high performance in identifying COVID-19 and symptom events with associated assertion values (0.83-0.97 F1 for events and 0.73-0.79 F1 for assertions).
label: none

sentence: Our span-based event extraction model outperforms an extractor built on MetaMapLite for the identiﬁcation of symptoms with assertion values.
label: none

sentence: In a secondary use application, we predicted COVID-19 test results using structured patient data (e.g. vital signs and laboratory results) and automatically extracted symptom information, to explore the clinical presentation of COVID-19.
label: none

sentence: Automatically extracted symptoms improve COVID-19 prediction performance, beyond structured data alone.
label: none

sentence: Keywords: COVID-19; coronavirus; machine learning; natural language processing; information extraction 1.
label: none

sentence: Introduction As of December 20, 2020, there were over 75 million conﬁrmed COVID-19 cases globally, resulting in 1.6 million related deaths [ 1 ].
label: none

sentence: Surveillance efforts to track the spread of COVID-19 and estimate the true number of infections remains a challenge for policy makers, healthcare workers, and researchers, even as testing availability increases.
label: none

sentence: Symptom information provides useful indicators for tracking potential COVID-19 infections and disease clusters [ 2 ].
label: none

sentence: Certain symptoms and underlying comorbidities have directed COVID-19 ∗ Corresponding author Email address: lybarger@uw.edu (Kevin Lybarger) Preprint submitted to arXiv March 12, 2021 testing.
label: none

sentence: However, the clinical presentation of COVID-19 varies signiﬁcantly in severity and symptom proﬁles [3].
label: none

sentence: The most prevalent COVID-19 symptoms reported to date are fever, cough, fatigue, and dyspnea [ 4 ], but emerging reports identify additional symptoms, including diarrhea and neurological symptoms, such as changes in taste or smell [ 5 – 7 ].
label: none

sentence: Certain initial symptoms may be associated with higher risk of complications; in one study, dyspnea was associated with a two-fold increased risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome [ 8 ].
label: none

sentence: However, correlations between symptoms, positive tests, and rapid clinical deterioration are not well understood in ambulatory care and emergency department settings.
label: none

sentence: Routinely collected information in the Electronic Health Record (EHR) can provide crucial COVID-19 testing, diagnosis, and symptom data needed to address these knowledge gaps.
label: none

sentence: Laboratory results, vital signs, and other structured data results can easily be queried and analyzed at scale; however, more detailed and nuanced descriptions of COVID-19 diagnoses, exposure history, symptoms, and clinical decision-making are typically only documented in the clinical narrative.
label: none

sentence: To leverage this textual information in large-scale studies, the salient COVID-19 and symptom information must be automatically extracted.
label: none

sentence: This work presents a new corpus of clinical text annotated for COVID-19, referred to as the COVID-19 Annotated Clinical Text (CACT) Corpus.
label: none

sentence: CACT consists of 1,472 notes from the University of Washing- ton (UW) clinical repository with detailed event-based annotations for COVID-19 diagnosis, testing, and symptoms.
label: none

sentence: The event-based annotations characterize these phenomena across multiple dimensions, including assertion, severity, change, and other attributes needed to comprehensively represent these clinical phenomena in secondary use applications.
label: none

sentence: This work is part of a larger effort to use routinely collected data describing the clinical presentation of acute and chronic diseases, with two major aims; 1) to describe the presence, character, and changes in symptoms associated with clinical conditions, where delays or misdiagnoses occur in clinical practice and impact patient outcomes (e.g. infectious diseases, cancer) [ 9 ], and 2) to provide a more efﬁcient and cost-effective mechanism to validate clinical prediction rules previously derived from large prospective cohort studies [ 10 ].
label: none

sentence: To the best of our knowledge, CACT is the ﬁrst clinical data set with COVID-19 annotations, and it includes 29.9K distinct events.
label: none

sentence: We present the ﬁrst information extraction results on CACT using an end-to-end neural event extraction model, establishing a strong baseline for identifying COVID-19 and symptom events.
label: none

sentence: We explore the prediction of COVID-19 test results (positive or negative) using structured EHR data and automatically extracted symptoms and ﬁnd that the automatically extracted symptoms improve prediction performance. 2.
label: none

sentence: Annotated Corpora Given the recent onset of COVID-19, there are limited COVID-19 corpora for natural language processing (NLP) experimentation.
label: none

sentence: Corpora of scientiﬁc papers related to COVID-19 are available [ 11 , 12 ], and automatic 2 labels for biomedical entity types are available for some of these research papers [ 13 ].
label: none

sentence: However, we are unaware of corpora of clinical text with supervised COVID-19 annotations.
label: none

sentence: Multiple clinical corpora are annotated for symptoms.
label: none

sentence: As examples, South et al. [14] annotated symptoms and other medical concepts with negation (present/not present), temporality, and other attributes.
label: none

sentence: Koeling et al. [15] annotated a pre-deﬁned set of symptoms related to ovarian cancer.
label: none

sentence: For the i2b2/VA challenge, Uzuner et al. [16] annotated medical concepts, including symptoms, with assertion values and relations.
label: none

sentence: While some of these corpora may include symptom annotations relevant to COVID-19 (e.g. “cough” or “fever”), the distribution and characterization of symptoms in these corpora may not be consistent with COVID-19 presentation.
label: none

sentence: To ﬁll the gap in clinical COVID-19 annotations and detailed symptom annotation, we introduce CACT to provide a relatively large corpus with COVID-19 diagnosis, testing, and symptom annotations. 2.2.
label: none

sentence: Medical Concept and Symptom Extraction The most commonly used United Medical Language System (UMLS) concept extraction systems are the clinical Text Analysis and Knowledge Extraction System (cTAKES) [ 17 ] and MetaMap [ 18 ].
label: none

sentence: The National Library of Medicine (NLM) created a lightweight Java implementation of MetaMap, MetaMapLite , which demonstrated real-time speed and extraction performance comparable to or exceeding the performance of MetaMap, cTAKES, and DNorm [ 19 ].
label: none

sentence: In previous work, we built on MetaMapLite, incorporating assertion value predictions (e.g. present versus absent) using classiﬁers trained on the 2010 i2b2 challenge dataset to create the extraction pipeline referred to here as MetaMapLite++ [ 20 ].
label: none

sentence: MetaMapLite++ assigns each extracted UMLS Metathesaurus concept an assertion value with an Support Vector Machine (SVM)-based assertion classiﬁer that utilizes syntactic and semantic knowledge.
label: none

sentence: The SVM assertion classiﬁer achieved state-of-the-art assertion performance (Micro-F1 94.23) on the i2b2 2010 assertion dataset [ 21 ].
label: none

sentence: Here, we use MetaMapLite++ as a baseline for evaluating extraction performance for a subset of our annotated phenomena, speciﬁcally symptoms with assertion values, using the UMLS “Sign or Symptom” semantic type.
label: none

sentence: The Mayo Clinic updated its rule-based medical tagging system, MedTagger [ 22 ], to include a COVID-19 speciﬁc module that extracts 18 phenomena related to COVID-19, including 11 common COVID-19 symptoms with assertion values [23].
label: none

sentence: We do not use the COVID-19 MedTagger variant as a baseline, because our symptom annotation and extraction is not limited to known COVID-19 symptoms. 2.3.
label: none

sentence: Relation and Event Extraction There is a signiﬁcant body of information extraction (IE) work related to coreference resolution, relation extraction, and event extraction tasks.
label: none

sentence: In these tasks, spans of interest are identiﬁed, and linkages between spans are predicted.
label: none

sentence: Many contemporary IE systems use end-to-end multi-layer neural models that encode an input word sequence using recurrent or transformer layers, classify spans (entities, arguments, etc.), and predict the relationship between spans (coreference, relation, role, etc.) [ 24 – 29 ].
label: none

sentence: Of most relevance to our work is a series of developments starting with Lee et al. [30] , which introduces a span-based coreference resolution model that enumerates all spans in a word sequence, predicts entities using a feed-forward neural 3 network (FFNN) operating on span representations, and resolves coreferences using a FFNN operating on entity span-pairs.
label: none

sentence: Luan et al. [31] adapts this framework to entity and relation extraction, with a speciﬁc focus on scientiﬁc literature.
label: none

sentence: Luan et al. [32] extends the method to take advantage both of co-reference and relation links in a graph-based approach to jointly predict entity spans, co-reference, and relations.
label: none

sentence: By updating span representations in multi-sentence co-reference chains, the graph-based approach achieved state-of-the-art on several IE tasks representing a range of different genres.
label: none

sentence: Wadden et al. [33] expands on Luan et al. [32] ’s approach, adapting it to event extraction tasks.
label: none

sentence: We build on Luan et al. [31] and Wadden et al. [33] ’s work, augmenting the modeling framework to ﬁt the CACT annotation scheme.
label: none

sentence: In CACT, event arguments are generally close to the associated trigger, and inter-sentence events linked by co-reference are infrequent, so the graph-based extension, which adds complexity, is unlikely to beneﬁt our extraction task.
label: none

sentence: Many recent NLP systems use pre-trained language models (LMs), such as ELMo, BERT, and XLNet, that leverage unannotated text [ 34 – 36 ].
label: none

sentence: A variety of strategies for incorporating the LM output are used in IE systems, including using the contextualized word embedding sequence: as the input to a Conditional Random Field entity extraction layer [ 37 ], as the basis for building span representations [ 32 , 33 ], or by adding an entity-aware attention mechanism and pooled output states to a fully transformer-based model [ 38 ].
label: none

sentence: There are many domain-speciﬁc LM variants.
label: none

sentence: Here, we use Alsentzer et al. [39] ’s Bio+Clinical BERT , which is trained on PubMed papers and MIMIC-III [40] clinical notes. 2.4.

sentence: COVID-19 Outcome Prediction There are many pre-print and published works exploring the prediction of COVID-19 outcomes, including COVID-19 infection, hospitalization, acute respiratory distress syndrome, need for intensive care unit (ICU), need for a ventilator, and mortality [ 41 – 53 ].

sentence: Data An existing clinical data set from the UW from January 2020 through May 2020 was used to explore the prediction of COVID-19 test results and identify the most prominent predictors of COVID-19.

label: none

label: none

sentence: For each patient in this data set, all of the COVID-19 tests with either a positive or negative result and at least one note within the seven days preceding the test result were identiﬁed.
label: none

sentence: Only COVID-19 tests with a note within the previous seven days are included in experimentation, to improve the robustness of the COVID-19 symptomology exploration.

sentence: Each of these test results was treated as a sample in this binary classiﬁcation task (positive or negative).

sentence: The likelihood of COVID-19 positivity was predicted using structured EHR data and notes within a 7-day window preceding the test result.

sentence: Conclusions We present CACT, a novel corpus with detailed annotations for COVID-19 diagnoses, testing, and symptoms.
label: none

sentence: CACT includes 1,472 unique notes across six note types with more than 500 notes from patients with future positive COVID-19 tests.
label: none

sentence: We implement the Span-based Event Extractor, which jointly extracts 19 all annotated phenomena, including argument types and subtypes.
label: none

sentence: The Span-based Event Extractor achieves near-human performance in the extraction of COVID triggers (0.97 F1) and Symptom triggers (0.83 F1) and Assertions (0.79 F1).
label: none

sentence: The performance of several attributes (e.g. Change , Severity , Characteristics , Duration , and Frequency ) is lower than that of Assertion .
label: none

sentence: This lower performance may partly be due to the focus on COVID-19, where clinicians’ notes: 1) are highly structured around the presence/absence of a certain set of symptoms, 2) usually describe a single consultation per patient within 7 days of COVID-19 testing, and 3) focus on assessing the need for COVID-19 testing and in-person ambulatory or ED care.
label: none

sentence: In a COVID-19 prediction task, automatically extracted symptom information improved the prediction of COVID-19 test results (with signiﬁcance) beyond just using structured data, and the top predictive symptoms include fever, cough, and myalgia.
label: none

sentence: CACT only includes notes from early in the COVID-19 pandemic (February-March 2020), and our understanding of the presentation of COVID-19 has evolved since that time.
label: none

sentence: CACT was annotated for all symptoms described in the clinical narrative, not just known symptoms of COVID-19, so the annotated symptoms cover most of the symptoms currently known to be associated with COVID-19.
label: none

sentence: However, CACT includes infrequent references to losses of taste or smell.
label: none

sentence: In future work, the extractor will be applied to a much larger set of clinical ambulatory care and ED notes from UW.
label: none

sentence: The extracted symptom information will be combined with routinely coded data (e.g. diagnosis and procedure codes, demographics) and automatically extracted data (e.g. social determinants of health [ 61 ]).
label: none

sentence: These models could better inform clinical indications for prioritizing testing, and the presence or absence of certain symptoms can be used to inform clinical care decisions with greater precision.
label: none

sentence: This future work may also identify combinations of symptoms (including their presence, absence, severity, sequence of appearance, duration, etc.) associated with clinical outcomes and health service utilization, such as deteriorating clinical course and need for repeat consultation or hospital admission.
label: none

sentence: The use of detailed symptom information will be highly valuable in informing these models, but potentially only with the level of nuance that our extraction models provide.
label: none

sentence: For the COVID-19 pandemic, we anticipate that the extraction model presented here will be of increasing value to clinical researchers, as the need to distinguish COVID-19 from other viral and bacterial respiratory infections becomes more necessary.
label: none

sentence: As the pandemic subsides with widespread vaccination, we will return to the more typical “winter respiratory infection/inﬂuenza” seasons, where routine medical care involves differentiating COVID-19 from many other types of viral infections and identifying individuals that require COVID-19 testing.
label: none

sentence: Symptom extraction models, like the model presented here, may provide the data needed to determine risk of certain infections and triage the need for testing.
label: none

sentence: We intend to explore the value of this symptom annotation scheme and extraction approach for clinical conditions where multiple consultations lead to a time point in the diagnosis pathway and symptom attributes, like change and severity, are even more important.
label: none

sentence: We are especially interested in medical conditions for which delayed or missed diagnoses are known to lead to patient harm [ 9 ].
label: none

sentence: We intend to examine data sets 20 associated with other acute and chronic conditions to investigate symptom patterns that could be used to more efﬁciently and accurately identify patients with these conditions.

sentence: Speciﬁcally, we intend to further develop the symptom extractor to reduce diagnostic delay for lung cancer, which is known to present at a later stage.

sentence: Lung cancer diagnosis often occurs after many consultations in ambulatory settings, and there may be opportunities to more quickly identify high-risk individuals based on symptoms.

sentence: Sabuncu https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7068-719X msabuncu@cornell.edu arXiv:2210.07416v2 [cs.LG] 18 Dec 2024 ECE Department, Cornell Tech, New York, NY, USA ∗ for the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative Abstract The Granger framework is useful for discovering causal relations in time-varying signals.

sentence: However, most Granger causality (GC) methods are developed for densely sampled time- series data.
label: none

sentence: A substantially different setting, particularly common in medical imaging, is the longitudinal study design, where multiple subjects are followed and sparsely observed over time.
label: none

sentence: Longitudinal studies commonly track several biomarkers, which are likely gov- erned by nonlinear dynamics that might have subject-specific idiosyncrasies and exhibit both direct and indirect causes.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, real-world longitudinal data often suffer from widespread missingness.
label: none

sentence: GC methods are not well-suited to handle these issues.
label: none

sentence: In this paper, we propose an approach named GLACIAL (Granger and LeArning-based CausalIty Analysis for Longitudinal studies) to fill this methodological gap by marrying GC with a multi-task neural forecasting model.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL treats subjects as independent samples and uses the model’s average prediction accuracy on hold-out subjects to probe causal links.
label: none

sentence: Input dropout and model interpolation are used to efficiently learn nonlinear dynamic relationships between a large number of variables and to handle missing values respectively.
label: none

sentence: Extensive simulations and experiments on a real longitudinal medical imaging dataset show GLACIAL beating competitive baselines and confirm its utility.

sentence: Introduction Granger causality (GC) (Granger, 1969) is a versatile and popular framework that exploits “the arrow of time” to detect causal relations in timeseries data (Roebroeck et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2011).
label: none

sentence: In GC, we test whether past values of one time series predict the future values of another series (i.e., forecasting), which allows us to infer causal relationships.
label: none

sentence: Despite its popularity, current implementations of GC are only well-suited for densely and ∗ .

sentence: They are not designed for the longitudinal setup involving multiple systems (e.g., subjects), which are common in medical imaging.
label: none

sentence: Although one could infer a causal graph for each subject and aggregate the graphs across subjects, this approach is untenable in many longitudinal studies in medicine where each subject only has a few observations, making the inference of each causal graph inaccurate.
label: none

sentence: Constraint-based methods such as PC or FCI (Spirtes et al., 2000), which rely on in- dependent samples and conditional independence tests, are also commonly used for causal discovery.
label: none

sentence: These methods would use one observation per subject and thus are not designed to detect causal relations reflected in temporal dynamics.
label: none

sentence: We believe there is a lack of methods for causal discovery in longitudinal studies that consist of multiple subjects with sparse observations.
label: none

sentence: Longitudinal imaging studies typically track several variables simultaneously.
label: none

sentence: Thus, applying causal discovery to longitudinal studies can be challenging because of the large number of variables involved and the complex (nonlinear) relationships between variables.
label: none

sentence: Nonlinear GC methods (e.g. those based on non-parametric methods (Su and White, 2007; Marinazzo et al., 2008)) do not scale to large number of variables (Eichler, 2012).
label: none

sentence: Simi- larly, existing GC tests that use neural networks to infer nonlinear dynamics (Tank et al., 2021; Nauta et al., 2019; Khanna and Tan, 2020) also face scalability issues.
label: none

sentence: On the other hand, using linear GC to infer nonlinear relationships can be fast but may produce wrong results (Li et al., 2018).
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, prior GC methods are, to the best of our knowledge, all association-based.
label: none

sentence: That is, they test for causal relationships via interrogating fit (learned) model weights.
label: none

sentence: For example, in the linear GC approaches, this is achieved by testing the statistical significance of model coefficients.
label: none

sentence: As the detection power of association-based GC (Granger, 1969; L¨utkepohl, 2005) diminishes with increasing number of variables (Sugihara et al., 2012; Runge et al., 2019b), it may fail to detect the weak coupling between a node and its parents, in particular when there are a lot of variables and limited data (Runge et al., 2019a; Yuan and Shou, 2022).
label: none

sentence: Another challenge of real-world longitudinal studies is missing data.
label: none

sentence: While there is no consensus about what to do about missing values (Glymour et al., 2019), several works (Strobl et al., 2018; Tu et al., 2019) have tried to address this issue for cross- sectional data.
label: none

sentence: Yet, as far as we know, missingness is under-explored in longitudinal studies, particularly in the context of causal discovery.
label: none

sentence: Finally, GC, in its original form, does not differentiate between direct and indirect causes (Yuan and Shou, 2022).
label: none

sentence: Although, in theory, infinite history (observations) could shield off indirect causes from being detected as edges in the output causal graph, when the number of observations per subject is small, false positives due to indirect causes is a common practical problem.
label: none

sentence: In this work, we propose GLACIAL (Fig 1), which stands for a “Granger and LeArning- based CausalIty Analysis for Longitudinal studies.” GLACIAL combines GC with a practi- cal machine-learning based approach to test for causal relations among multiple variables in a longitudinal study.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL extends GC to longitudinal studies by treating each sub- ject’s trajectory as an independent sample, governed by a shared causal mechanism that is reflected in the temporal dynamics.
label: none

sentence: This treatment is similar to prior works where subjects are assumed to be independent samples in longitudinal data analysis (Hernan and Robins, 2020).
label: none

sentence: Critically, GLACIAL infers causal relation- ships based on interrogating predictive accuracy and not a direct analysis of model weights, which is common in existing association-based GC methods.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL employs a single multi-task neural forecasting model, trained with input feature drop-out, to learn nonlinear relationships among all variables in time-varying data.
label: none

sentence: The model also handles missing values using model interpolation.
label: none

sentence: Thus, although neural networks have been used in the past for causal discovery, GLACIAL efficiently tests for causal relations of a large set of variables in data where timepoints may be sampled irregularly and may contain missing values.
label: none

sentence: The efficiency and flexibility of GLACIAL make it applicable to real-world multi- modal medical imaging studies with many variables.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, GLACIAL includes post-processing heuristics to account for indirect causes and resolve the directionality of detected ambiguous associations.
label: none

sentence: Extensive experiments on synthetic data and real data from a longitudinal medical imaging study show that GLACIAL can infer relationships ac- curately even in challenging real-world scenarios with sparse observations, a large number of variables and direct causes, and a large degree of missing data.

sentence: Related Works Most existing causal discovery (CD) methods are not intended for the longitudinal study design, where multiple subjects are sparsely observed at different timepoints.
label: none

sentence: CD methods designed for timeseries data or independent samples are often used in the longitudinal setting despite potential poor performance.
label: none

sentence: Causal Discovery: CD methods intended for cross-sectional studies are ill-suited for longitudinal studies.
label: none

sentence: Search methods can scale well if causal relations are linear (Kalisch and B¨uhlman, 2007; Ramsey et al., 2017) although their output may not be informative enough (e.g. containing bidirectional edges).
label: none

sentence: In contrast, by making strong assumptions about the functional form of the causal process, FCM can better identify the causal direction (Hyv¨arinen and Pajunen, 1999; Zhang et al., 2015), although FCM methods usually do not scale well (Glymour et al., 2019).
label: none

sentence: Besides, if the assumed FCM is too restrictive to be able to approximate the true data generating process, the results may be misleading.
label: none

sentence: There are also various CD methods for timeseries (Chu et al., 2008; Runge et al., 2019b; Runge, 2020; Entner and Hoyer, 2010; Malinsky and Spirtes, 2018, 2019; Hyv¨arinen et al., 2010; Peters et al., 2013; Pamfil et al., 2020).
label: none

sentence: These methods take in consecutive blocks of observations and output a Full Time Graph (Peters et al., 2017), which contain not only the variables in the system but also their temporally-lagged versions.
label: none

sentence: Although methods for timeseries may be better than cross-sectional ones, they are still not ideal for longitudinal data where sparse observations with potentially missing values come from more than one subject.
label: none

sentence: Granger Causality: GC (Granger, 1969, 1980) checks for dependence between vari- ables’ timeseries, after accounting for other available information.
label: none

sentence: Temporal dependence is thus linked to causation by the “Common Cause Principle”: two dependent variables are causally related (one causes the other, or both share a common cause) (Peters et al., 2017).
label: none

sentence: Checking pairwise dependence in GC can be efficient, but often yields false positives be- cause other variables in the system are not accounted for.
label: none

sentence: In contrast, multivariate GC can account for common causes and therefore is more accurate but also more computationally demanding (Eichler, 2007, 2012).
label: none

sentence: In practice, multivariate GC may be infeasible for a large set of variables and more efficient approaches (Basu et al., 2015; Huang and Kleinberg, 2015) were developed to deal with this challenge.
label: none

sentence: Recently, more general GC tests based on neural networks (Tank et al., 2021; Nauta et al., 2019; Khanna and Tan, 2020) have been proposed which outperform vector auto regressive (VAR) linear GC (Glymour et al., 2019).
label: none

sentence: Scaling these neural-network based GC methods to handle a large number of variables is still a concern.
label: none

sentence: Missing data: For cross-sectional studies, missing values can be imputed, which may result in data contradicting the causal processes if imputation is done naively.
label: none

sentence: Al- ternatively, observations with missing values can be removed (list-wise deletion), which can lead to the omission of vast amounts of valuable datapoints.
label: none

sentence: Test-wise Deletion PC (TDPC) (Strobl et al., 2018) is more data-efficient than list-wise deletion but may produce spurious edges when missingness is not completely at random (Tu et al., 2019).
label: none

sentence: Missing- Value PC (MVPC) (Tu et al., 2019) corrects TDPC’s output to account for different miss- ingness scenarios.
label: none

sentence: Although, tackling missingness in data through imputation has been studied extensively (Ma et al., 2019, 2020; Ma and Zhang, 2021; Morales-Alvarez et al., 2022) in the context of cross-sectional studies, to the best of our knowledge, no existing method addresses missingness in longitudinal studies for the CD task. 2226 Granger and Learning-based Causality Analysis for Longitudinal Imaging Studies 3.
label: none

sentence: Method Both cross-sectional CD methods (multiple subject, single timepoint data) and timeseries CD methods (single subject, multiple timepoints data) are ill-suited for longitudinal studies (multiple subjects, multiple timepoints data).
label: none

sentence: Besides, prior methods often assume time- series are infinitely long (i.e. unlimited history), regularly sampled, and without missing values.
label: none

sentence: Thus, they may not work for real-world datasets when observation history per sub- ject is limited, irregular, and riddled with missing values.
label: none

sentence: The next few sections show (1) how GLACIAL handles longitudinal data, (2) how GLACIAL deals with irregularly sam- pled timepoints containing missing values, and (3) GLACIAL’s post-processing strategies to account for limited history of observed timeseries.

sentence: Discussion Longitudinal studies, in which multiple subjects are sparsely observed for a limited num- ber of times, are particularly common in population health applications.
label: none

sentence: Longitudinal studies often track many variables, which are likely governed by nonlinear dynamics that might have subject-specific idiosyncrasies.
label: none

sentence: Yet, longitudinal studies are not amenable to the popular Granger causality (GC) analysis, since GC was developed to analyze a single mul- 2237 Nguyen et al. Figure 8: Baseline approaches’ predicted interaction of ADNI biomarkers. tivariate densely sampled timeseries.
label: none

sentence: Furthermore, real-world longitudinal data often suffer from widespread missingness.
label: none

sentence: We developed GLACIAL which combines the GC framework with a machine learning based prediction model to address the need for a method to find causal relations of numerous variables in longitudinal multi-modal medical imaging studies.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL treats subjects as independent samples and uses average prediction accuracy on hold-out subjects to test for causal relations.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL exploits a single multi-task neural network trained with input feature dropout to efficiently probe links.
label: none

sentence: GLACIAL places no restriction on the design of the neural network predictor.
label: none

sentence: Although we showed GLACIAL working well in many settings (varying lag-times, noise levels, and missingness degree), there are some questions remaining that need further in- vestigation.
label: none

sentence: Even though the ADNI dataset is small by machine learning standard, many scientific datasets are even smaller so characterizing the performance on small datasets would be interesting.
label: none

sentence: In addition, it would be interesting to use GLACIAL to analyze more medical imaging datasets (Guti´errez-Z´u˜niga et al., 2022; Basaia et al., 2022).
label: none

sentence: We focused on continuous variables since they are the most common but extending GLACIAL to dis- crete variables by adopting techniques in (Peters et al., 2010; Cai et al., 2018; Huang et al., 2018) would make GLACIAL analysis applicable to more longitudinal studies.
label: none

sentence: Further- more, studying GLACIAL’s behaviors under missingness other than MCAR is important despite GLACIAL outputting plausible graphs on real-world data (ADNI).
label: none

sentence: Missing at ran- dom (MAR; missingness probabilities depend on the values of the observed features) and missing not at random (MNAR; missingness depends on the values of the ,unobserved fea- tures) are different from MCAR, and MNAR in particular may require different treatments.
label: none

sentence: Besides, GLACIAL assumes that there is no feedback, hidden confounder, or instantaneous effect.
label: none

sentence: Thus, before applying GLACIAL, it is critical to verify whether these assumptions are reasonable to ensure that causal relations inferred by GLACIAL are valid.
label: none

sentence: The third assumption in particular requires that the sampling resolution is high enough to capture transient changes (e.g. impulses) or temporal orderings between causal pairs with short time lags.
label: none

sentence: Similar to other causal discovery methods, GLACIAL can offer valuable insights into relationships between variables.
label: none

sentence: However, intentional or unintentional misuse may lead to harmful consequences.
label: none

sentence: Causal discovery methods, such as GLACIAL, identify potential causal links based on statistical patterns in the data, so biased data collection may lead to misleading findings.
label: none

sentence: These flawed findings may further lead to misguided medical treatments or clinical decisions that can harm vulnerable populations.
label: none

sentence: Moreover, violations of modeling assumptions and measurement errors can contribute to mistakes in the inferred graphs.
label: none

sentence: Thus, it is important to ensure unbiased data collection as well as to corroborate any identified causal links using further experimentation and follow-up study designs to mitigate potential risks when applying causal discovery.
